lunchwine/space-trader-classic.readme:
# Space Trader Classic

A web port of Russell Wolf's (aka Brucelet) Android port of Pieter Spronck's PalmOS game, **Space Trader**. This version was directly adapted from Russell Wolf's v1.3.5, and attempts to be a faithful port. The only features added are import/export of save games and system-based light/dark mode.

The entire game has been ported to HTML/JS/CSS and can be run as an Android native app (via web wrapper), in-browser, or as a Progressive Web App (PWA). To play in browser or install as a PWA, visit https://spacetrader.lunchwine.com.

Full disclosure: the majority of the work was porting the previous Java codebase to HTML/JS, and nearly all of that coding was done by LLMs (with human testing and direction). My goal was to bring back a classic that had brought me many hours of joy, dating back to the PalmOS version in the early 00s, and make it accessible to more people.

This project is actively maintained: builds are kept working and significant bugs are fixed. Issues are welcome, but there is no guaranteed response or personal support.

## Play

Open **index.html** in a current browser. It has no dependencies and works offline. To serve it instead:

```
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Tap the screen title to open the menu bar: **Command** (screens), **Game** (New Game, Switch Game, Retire,
Options, Shortcuts, High Scores, Export Save, Import Save) and **Help**. Progress is saved automatically in the
browser; Export Save and Import Save move a game between devices. Two games can be kept at once (Switch Game).

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | The built game: everything inlined (code, images, fonts). |
| `src/engine.js` | Rules, travel, combat, quests and the save model. |
| `src/generation.js` | Galaxy and opponent generation. |
| `src/encounters.js`, `src/campaigns.js`, `src/yard.js`, `src/finishing.js` | Encounters, quest campaigns, shipyard, endings. |
| `src/data.js`, `src/data.json`, `src/presentation-data.js` | Game constants, names and strings. |
| `src/ui.js`, `src/style.css`, `src/page.html` | The player interface and page template. |
| `assets/` | Original artwork (PNG masters, WebP copies) and Roboto fonts. |
| `android/` | Android WebView wrapper (Gradle project, package `io.github.lunchwine.spacetraderclassic`). |
| `pwa/` | Web app manifest, service worker and icons for the PWA. |
| `fastlane/` | F-Droid store metadata (descriptions, changelogs, screenshots). |
| `scripts/` | `build.py` (bundle) and `to_webp.cjs` (image conversion). |
| `tests/` | Engine integration tests and browser tests; `tests/fixtures/` holds sample saves. |

## Build

Python 3 only. After changing anything in `src/` or `assets/`:

```
python3 scripts/build.py
```

This rewrites `index.html`. If you change a PNG in `assets/`, run `node scripts/to_webp.cjs` first; the build
embeds the WebP copy when it is smaller than the PNG.

`node scripts/render_icons.cjs` regenerates the launcher, PWA and fastlane icon PNGs from the SVG masters in `art/`.

### Android

Needs OpenJDK 17, Android SDK platform 35, build-tools 35.0.0 and Python 3 (set `JAVA_HOME` and `ANDROID_HOME`):

```
cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease
```

Gradle runs `scripts/build.py` itself. The unsigned APK is `android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk`.
`./gradlew assembleDebug` makes a debug-signed APK that can be sideloaded. `android/dev-env.sh` is an optional local helper that sets the
environment.

### Releasing

Bump `version` in package.json and `versionName`/`versionCode` in `android/app/build.gradle` together (`build.py` enforces it;

# 🏁 CarRace **A Formula-style racing game that runs in your browser. Built on Three.js. No build step, no assets, no installs.** ### [▶ PLAY NOW](https://alexander-uspenskiy.github.io/CarRace/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-e10600?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE) [![Three.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.js-r170-000000?style=for-the-badge&logo=threedotjs&logoColor=white)](https://threejs.org) [![No build step](https://img.shields.io/badge/build%20step-none-2ea44f?style=for-the-badge)](#-quick-start) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-330%2B%20passing-2ea44f?style=for-the-badge)](#-tests) **3 circuits · 10 teams · 20-car grid · 5 to 10 minute races · upgrades · Hall of Fame**
--- ## 🎮 What is it? Pick a team from the **2025 Formula grid**, choose a circuit and a race length (5, 7 or 10 minutes), spend your credits in the garage, and race 19 AI drivers for the podium. Everything you see and hear is generated in code: the cars, the tracks, the textures, even the engine sound.

Title: your driver name, credits and the Ferrari SF-25 on the turntable
Team select: 10 teams, 20 drivers, each with its own stats and livery

Three circuits, each with a different character and your best laps
Garage: spend credits on engine, aero, brakes, tyres and cooling

Cockpit camera (press C): halo, front wheels and the pack ahead
Podium: results, credits earned and new Hall of Fame records
## ✨ Features - 🏎️ **2025 grid.** 10 teams and 20 drivers, each with its own car stats and livery. The lap count is calculated per track so the race lasts about as long as you chose. Easy, Normal and Hard AI. - 🔧 **Car upgrades.** Engine, aero, brakes, tyres and cooling at levels 0 to 5, paid with credits you earn from results. # Riyadh Kids Adventures

Family-friendly Godot 4 game: drive the blue Mazda CX-9 around Riyadh as Daniah, Sarah or Lamia,
visit Tamimi Supermarket, School, Home (3 zones) and take the road trip to the Al-Muzahimiyah farm.

* Design: [docs/GDD.md](docs/GDD.md)
* Engine: Godot 4.3+ (GDScript). Open this folder in Godot (first open imports the project and registers the `class_name` scripts), then press **F5**.
  Headless check: `godot --headless --import`.

**Controls:** W/S gas & brake (hold S to reverse), A/D steer, **SPACE handbrake** (tap it while turning with the gas on for a *Driver*-style slide; the tyres leave skid marks and smoke), **C** camera (chase / far / hood; orbit with right-mouse drag or J/L/I/K, zoom with wheel or U/O, B looks back, V locks), **E** enter a light-beam location (slow down first), Esc back to menu/skip. Gamepad supported.

**Crashes:** hit walls or cars hard and the CX-9 gets damaged for real: dents, a crumpled hood and bumper, broken lights, cracked glass, steam, smoke and finally flames, plus less power and a pull to one side. The HUD shows `Car: %`. Repair it at **Mazda Service** (blue circle on the top-middle avenue) or by going home.

**Soundtrack:** Daniah = American rock, Sarah = Korean pop, Lamia = Arabic (maqam Hijaz). Generated in code. To play **your own song** for a sister: on the character screen press **Choose song...** under her name and pick an mp3/ogg (the choice is remembered), or put `lamia.mp3` etc. in the `music` folder.

**Farm:** pick an animal - **Shatoor the duck**, **Hassan the goat** or the chicken - then walk (WASD, SPACE jump) into the glowing circles to play. E enters.

**Farm games (7 + pool/ping-pong/basketball/cornhole):** the farm now has a **map** (top-right, press **M** for the big map), **families strolling around**, and these games - **Bottle Archery** (bow or air rifle at sand / water / Pepsi / Cola bottles, the wind pushes your shot, TAB switches weapon), **Swing Set** (pump with SPACE, jump with W), **Motorbike Track** (D gas, A brake, W/S tilt in the air), a **Pool** where your sister swims the crawl, **Basketball** where she takes the shots, and a **Cornhole match vs Dad** in perspective.

**Android:** the game has on-screen touch controls (a joystick or steer/GAS/BRAKE/DRIFT buttons, tap-to-click menus, finger-drag to aim and to orbit the camera) that appear automatically on a phone/tablet - and on a PC when you start it with `--touch`. A debug **APK** is built by GitHub on every push: open the repo's **Actions** tab -> latest "Android APK" run -> download `RiyadhKids-android-apk`, copy `RiyadhKids-debug.apk` to the phone and open it (allow "install unknown apps"). To build it yourself: `.\build_android.ps1 -Godot <path to Godot 4.3 exe>` (needs the export templates, Android Studio's SDK and JDK 17). Landscape only; best on a recent phone (arm64).

**Run it the safe way (Windows):** `.\run_game.ps1` imports new scripts first, starts the game and writes any errors to `game.log` - send me that file if something breaks.

**Try it:** Play → pick a sister → drive to the supermarket circle (NW) → press E.

**Tests (Godot 4.3):**
* `godot --headless res://tests/smoke_test.tscn` loads every scene, plays every mini-game and drives the car (headless prints harmless `mesh_get_surface_count` messages from the dummy renderer).
* `godot --headless res://tests/music_test.tscn -- <folder>` renders the three tracks to WAV files.
* `godot --headless res://tests/handling_test.tscn` checks handbrake turns, cornering and crash damage numbers.
* `res://tests/drive_shots.tscn`, `crash_shots.tscn`, `scene_tour.tscn` take screenshots (need a real renderer, e.g. xvfb).

All thirteen mini-games are playable greybox versions. `res://tests/farm_games_test.tscn` checks the new farm games headless.

ffawazz/NinjagoGame.readme:
# NINJAGO RUNNER - PS1 "Pepsiman"-style 3D runner (Python + Ursina)

Behind-the-back auto-runner: dodge, jump and slide through **3 levels** as
Kai, Jay, Cole, Zane or Lloyd. Launches **full screen** on Windows.
Runs with **zero assets** (everything is built from low-poly cubes, with an
animated fallback cutscene) - add your own models, music and videos any time.

## 1. Install (Windows, Python 3.9 - 3.12 recommended)

```bat
python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\activate
pip install ursina
python main.py
```
`ursina` pulls in `panda3d` (renderer, audio, video) automatically.
Use `python main.py --windowed` to debug in a window.
(Optional, to build an .exe: `pip install pyinstaller` then
`pyinstaller --onefile --noconsole --add-data "assets;assets" main.py`.)

## 2. Folder structure

```
NinjagoGame/
├── main.py          game loop, menu, HUD, states, player physics
├── config.py        ninjas, difficulties, levels, jokes, key bindings
├── entities.py      ninja model, obstacles, endless floor, scenery
├── ps1.py           PS1 shader (vertex snap, flat shading, 15-bit colour, fog)
├── cutscene.py      end-of-level video player + animated fallback
├── requirements.txt
└── assets/                     <- YOUR FILES GO HERE
    ├── music/
    │   ├── ninjago_theme.ogg   main looping soundtrack (.ogg/.mp3/.wav)
    │   ├── menu.ogg            (optional) menu track
    │   └── level1.ogg level2.ogg level3.ogg   (optional per-level tracks)
    ├── sfx/                    (all optional) jump, slide, stud, hit, win, lose (.wav/.ogg)
    ├── videos/
    │   └── level1.mp4  level2.mp4  level3.mp4   funny clips (played after each level)
    └── models/                 (optional) kai.glb  jay.glb  cole.glb  zane.glb  lloyd.glb
                                (.glb/.gltf/.obj/.bam; face +Z, feet at y=0, ~2 units tall)
```
The repo ships original placeholder chiptune music and sound effects (`assets/music/*.wav`, `assets/sfx/*.wav`, generated by `python tools/make_audio.py`). Drop your own `ninjago_theme.mp3`/`.ogg` in `assets/music/` and it takes priority over the `.wav` (the real Ninjago theme is copyrighted, so it is not included).
Every asset is optional. Missing music = silence, missing video = built-in
animated gag with captions, missing model = built-in blocky minifig ninja.
If an `.mp4` will not play, re-encode it:
`ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -profile:v baseline -c:a aac out.mp4`
(the game then falls back to the animated gag instead of crashing).

## 3. Controls

| Action | Keys |
|---|---|
| Menu | Up/Down = ninja, Left/Right = difficulty, Enter = start, Esc = quit (mouse works too) |
| Lane left / right | A / D or arrow keys |
| Jump (over low brick walls) | W / Up / Space |
| Slide (under beams) | S / Down / Ctrl / Shift (press in mid-air to fast-fall into a slide) |
| Dodge by changing lane | skull blocks |
| **Special power** | **E / F / left mouse** (costs energy; fills from studs, time and kills) |
| HD <-> retro PS1 look | F2 |
| Pause | Esc or P |
| Skip cutscene | Enter / Space / Esc |

## 3b. Skulkin enemies and ninja powers

Skeleton warriors (and tougher horned brutes from level 2) ambush you in a lane and
charge once you get close - dodge them or use your power. Each ninja has an element:

| Ninja | Power | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Kai | FIREBALL | explosive fireball, burns enemies over time |
| Jay | LIGHTNING | chain bolt hits the 3 nearest enemies |
| Cole | QUAKE | shockwave smashes enemies, rocks and walls |
| Zane | FREEZE | freezes all enemies ahead; run into a frozen one to shatter it |
| Lloyd | SPINJITZU | 3s tornado: invincible, smashes everything, pulls in studs |

Enemy frequency scales with difficulty and level (`enemy` / `enemy_chance` in `config.py`).
`config.GRAPHICS = 'HD'` (4x MSAA, full colour, no wobble) or `'RETRO'` (PS1 look).

## 4. How the requirements are met

* **Full screen / Windows**: `Ursina(fullscreen=True, borderless=True)` in `main.build_game`.
* **Pepsiman gameplay**: auto-run along +Z, 3

index.html     ゲームの案内ページ(GitHub Pagesのトップ)

f4lcon09/chess-teacher.readme:
# Chess Teacher

A personal chess teacher that runs entirely in the browser (no backend).

- Imports your games from the public chess.com API
- Analyzes them move by move with Stockfish (WASM, lite single-threaded)
- Classifies moves (best / good / inaccuracy / mistake / blunder) and gives rule-based explanations
- All data lives in your browser (IndexedDB)

Planned: opening statistics, bots to play against, a "mirror" bot that plays like you, puzzles.

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Stack

Vite, React, TypeScript, chess.js, react-chessboard, Dexie, Recharts, Stockfish.js.

## License notes

`public/stockfish/` contains an unmodified build of [Stockfish.js](https://github.com/nmrugg/stockfish.js)
(GPL-3.0, see `Copying.txt` in the npm package). Stockfish is a trademark of its authors.

jtwaugh/minceraft.desc: It's Taco Friday in voxel world! Operate the mince raft!
jtwaugh/minceraft.readme:
# minceraft **Mince Raft**, a small voxel game about living on a raft, and its world generator: a Beta-1.7.3-style overworld terrain generator written in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly, with a small browser viewer that renders it using the game's own 8×8 tileset. The game itself is being built here, phase by phase, from the design docs in [`docs/design/`](docs/design/). The generator is a clean-room implementation written from [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md), a prose description of the algorithm. No Mojang code or assets are in this repository (see [Clean-room rules](#clean-room-rules)). ## How this repo is built This project is built by a **software factory**: AI agents in GitHub Actions that turn ideas into reviewed pull requests, with one person deciding and merging. **[Read how it works and why →](FACTORY.md)** ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Idea"] --> B["Reconciler
checks it against the code"] B --> C["Design doc"] C --> D["Planner
small tickets + questions"] D --> E["Implementer
code + tests"] E --> F["CI + reviewer agent"] F --> G{"Maintainer merges"} G -->|phase done| D ``` - **The human decides, agents do the rest.** The maintainer writes ideas, answers questions (`/decide B`), picks tickets and merges. Agents can't approve or merge. - **Clean room by construction.** The decompiled game never leaves the maintainer's laptop, so the agents, running on GitHub, can't see it. They implement only from [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md), and CI blocks anything that looks like copied code. - **Ask, don't guess.** When a spec is unclear, agents open a question with options instead of picking one. - **A second agent reviews every PR** with fresh context, and CI checks formatting, lints, tests, wasm size, the flyover and the art. - **Docs stay true.** Design docs record what exists, phases are marked done when the code proves it, and a weekly job flags drift. ## Quick start ```sh ./build.sh --serve # build the wasm, then serve the viewer # open http://localhost:8000 ``` Requirements: Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, `wasm-pack`, and `wasm-opt` (binaryen). On macOS: ```sh rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown arch -arm64 brew install wasm-pack binaryen ``` `build.sh` options: | Command | Does | |---|---| | `./build.sh` | export textures, build the wasm, run `wasm-opt -Oz`, print its size | | `./build.sh --test` | run `cargo test` first | | `./build.sh --serve` | serve `viewer/` on port 8000 afterwards | ## Repository layout ``` SPEC.md algorithm spec the generator is implemented from build.sh build script (see above) art/ PROMPT.md prompt and palette for the pixel-art textures batches_*.json the tileset, one file per group of batches tools/ sheet builder, validator, export_textures.py data/ blocks.toml every block: id, name, fire values, collision, opacity, colour biomes.toml biome table, lookup thresholds, plant counts, tree shapes, spawn lists, our own grass/leaf/sky colour ramps crates/ terrain/ the generator: no_std + alloc, zero runtime dependencies build.rs turns data/*.toml into Rust constants at compile time src/climate.rs the one climate source + biome lookup src/decorate.rs decoration cells, passes, protected mask, snow src/trees.rs oak, birch, two taiga trees, big oak src/plants.rs flower / grass / dead bush / cane / cactus / pumpkin patches examples/stats.rs native timing, biome and vegetation statistics, PPM map web/ wasm-bindgen wrapper used by the viewer viewer/ index.html the viewer page (no frameworks) mesh.js block meshing, shared by the 3D view and the workers worker.js, pool.js background workers (map tiles, flyover plans and chunks) and their queue flyover/ flyover video: planner and player (see its README) pkg/

baratrion/gaffer.readme:
# Gaffer

A mobile-first football management game for the browser: one fictional club, one season, five-minute sessions.

**Play:** https://baratrion.github.io/gaffer/

## How it gets built
This repo is an experiment in "lights-off" software delivery. An unattended Claude Code factory, governed by [nWave](https://github.com/nWave-ai/nWave), builds the game a story at a time from scheduled GitHub Actions runs. The owner checks in once a week, from a phone.

- **nWave decides:** plan runs (DISCUSS + DESIGN) write the stories (`docs/roadmap.yaml`) and the technical decisions (`docs/product/architecture/`: stack, rendering, architecture), and nWave's reviewer agents critique them.
- **Done means evidence:** a story is complete only when its black-box scenarios in `tests/protected/` pass on `main`. Every scenario must fail on `main` when it is added, and it can never be edited afterwards.
- **Merge gates:** lint, types and tests through the stack's `ci:*` scripts; locked-path, append-only, test-count and diff-size guards; story regression; a phone-viewport smoke test; and an AI reviewer that can block. No human approval is needed.
- **Kill switch:** any open issue labelled `factory:stop`, or `"paused": true` in `factory/config.json`.

The research behind the design is in `docs/research/autonomous-delivery/`.

## Security note
The factory never reads Issue, PR or comment text. Steering happens only through owner commits and labels. Please don't file instructions as issues; they're ignored by design.

## Develop
```sh
pnpm install
pnpm dev
pnpm check && pnpm test:e2e
```

TraductorRenPy/TraductorRenPy.readme:
# TraductorRenPy

**Translate Ren'Py visual novels into your language, with one button.**
*(Versión en español: [README.es.md](README.es.md))*

![TraductorRenPy window](assets/screenshot-en.png)

TraductorRenPy takes a Ren'Py game, finds every line of text (dialogue, menus, buttons, notices…), translates
it with the AI engine of your choice, checks that nothing in the game can break, and installs the translation
back into the game — keeping a backup of everything it writes.

## Features

- **One-button mode** — "Translate this game automatically" runs every step and only asks what it must.
- **Guide list** — shows what is done (✓), what is next (▶), and remembers where you were between sessions.
- **Engines** — Gemini (has a free tier), Grok (xAI) and Microsoft Translator. Everyone uses **their own API key**.
- **Scene context** — the model sees the neighbouring lines and who is speaking, plus a per-game glossary
  (character names are kept; the game's title is never translated).
- **Safe by design** — every translated line is validated (tags `{i}`, variables `[name]`, `%s`, `\n`,
  quotes) before it is written; ids and comments never change; backups are made before writing.
- **Reuses earlier work** — import the translation of an older version (or a patch made by someone else) and
  translate only what is new or changed.
- **Finds unmarked texts** — `renpy.input` prompts, `text`/`textbutton` in screens, notifications… which Ren'Py
  does not extract by itself.
- **Works with `.rpa` archives** — extracts only scripts (without touching the game) and decompiles `.rpyc`
  with [unrpyc](https://github.com/CensoredUsername/unrpyc) (bundled, MIT).
- **8 target languages** built in (Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Russian, Polish, Turkish);
  any other Ren'Py language name can be typed in. Interface in **English and Spanish**.
- **API keys are stored encrypted** on your computer (Windows DPAPI), never inside the project.

## Quick start (Windows)

1. Download the latest `TraductorRenPy-…-windows.zip` from the **Releases** page and unzip it.
2. Install the free **Ren'Py SDK** from <https://www.renpy.org/latest.html> (the app finds it by itself, or use
   the *Find SDK* button).
3. Get an API key — the *Get key…* button opens the right page. Gemini has a free tier.
4. Run `TraductorRenPy.exe`, choose the game folder, choose the language and engine, paste your key and press
   **▶ Translate this game automatically**.
5. Open the game: it starts in the chosen language.

> Windows SmartScreen or your antivirus may warn about the `.exe` because it is not code-signed (this is common
> for small open-source tools built with PyInstaller). The full source is in this repository, and you can run it
> from source instead (see below).

Want to try it first? Use the included [`examples/demo_game`](examples/demo_game) (harmless original text).

### Run from source

Requires Python 3.9+ (Tk included in the standard installer). No extra packages are needed.

```bash
python main.py
```

## How it works

```
analyze → (extract .rpa → decompile .rpyc) → generate tl with the Ren'Py SDK → find unmarked texts
        → reuse earlier translation (optional) → translate with the engine → validate → install
```

Details for contributors: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## What it touches in your game

- It writes the translation into `game/tl/<language>/` and creates `game/zz_<language>.rpy`.
- Backups go to the work folder (`respaldos`). To undo, copy the backup back over `game/tl/<language>`.
- The game's own scripts are **never modified**. Optional cosmetic tweaks (dialogue box) live in a separate
  file, `game/zz_ui_tweaks.rpy`, that you can delete at any time.

## Known limitations

- Text **drawn inside images** (signs, backgrounds with letters) cannot be translated; only text the game writes
  as text.
- Quality depends on the engine you choose; machine translation always deserves a read-through.
- Tested on Windows 11 with P

# hello-eme-play

Turns **any website into a game**, configured by **one JSON**. The page itself is the playing field: the
visitor walks over it, punches paragraphs until they break, fights monsters, jumps on cards and drives a car.
It works with plain HTML, any framework and any CMS. An editor (one script, no framework) and a Payload plugin
change the JSON; try it in the [live demo](https://oldjazjef.github.io/hello-eme-play/): guide, editor and live preview.

![Top-down view: the figure fights monsters on a web page](docs/images/topdown.png)

## What it can do

- **Two views:** top-down and side-scroller (the figure and monsters are drawn in profile; page elements are platforms), switchable at any time by items, triggers or levels.
- **Figure, monsters, vehicles:** every one has stats (health, attack, speed, …), moves (punch, kick, bite) and a behavior (chase, wander, flee).
- **Levels and goals:** score, kills, survive for some time or defeat a boss.
- **Wave scripts and boss phases:** "at 10 s three blobs, at 25 s a swarm, at 40 s the boss"; a boss enrages or summons help when its health falls below a share.
- **Per-page settings:** `/blog` can be top-down and `/projects` a side-scroller, with other monsters; the game follows the visitor's navigation.
- **Items, upgrades and a shop**, **triggers** ("when X happens, if Y holds, do Z"), sounds and a high score.
- **Own pictures:** pixel art is built in; your own PNG or SVG sprite sheets with animations replace it.
- **Touch controls:** d-pad, round action buttons, steering wheel and pedals for the car.
- **Safe by design:** the JSON is always validated; wrong values are corrected, never crash the page.
- **An editor for the JSON:** quick settings, presets, a balance check, a live preview, a flow view and a guide, on any page or in Payload.

![Side-scroller view](docs/images/side-scroller.png)

| Package                                       | Purpose                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`@hello-eme/play`](packages/play)            | Browser runtime and drop-in script                                   |
| [`@hello-eme/play-core`](packages/core)       | Game logic without a DOM (entities, events, RNG)                     |
| [`@hello-eme/play-schema`](packages/schema)   | The JSON as data: defaults, validation, migrations, JSON Schema      |
| [`@hello-eme/play-editor`](packages/editor)   | The configuration editor for any page (one script), React export too |
| [`@hello-eme/play-payload`](packages/payload) | Payload CMS plugin: the same editor inside the Payload admin         |
| [`@hello-eme/play-sim`](packages/sim)         | Headless bots for balancing (`play-sim`)                             |
| [`examples/static`](examples/static)          | A plain HTML page with the game and Playwright tests (not published) |

## Get started in 5 minutes

**1. Add the script to your page.** Download `play.js` from the [latest release](https://github.com/oldjazjef/hello-eme-play/releases/latest) and put it next to your page (GitHub serves release files as downloads, so host it yourself):

```html
<script src="/play.js" data-config="{}" defer></script>
```

`{}` is a complete game: the classic one with all defaults.

**2. Start it.** The script adds a floating game button by itself (`data-toggle="off"` turns that off). Any button of yours can start and stop the game too:

**Preview in the CMS.** A page for the admin's live preview loads the script with `data-preview="https://cms.example.com"` (the admin's origin). It then plays whatever configuration the admin sends and starts a fresh round on every change; messages from other origins are ignored.

```html
<button type="button" data-play-toggle>Play</button>
```

commits.msg:
Make Voxunami 2048 infinite: a landscape of numbered blocks to push and merge

The ground is rolling hills in which every solid voxel is a numbered block (a
power of two) of stone, ice or spring ice. Players push and pull single blocks
with tools. Stone takes one step; ice coasts until it meets a block; spring ice
bounces back. A moving block that meets an equal number merges with it. Moving
blocks are entities acting in start order, saved with the world, so the
phased-tick rule is not needed fo

Add the network: TCP transport, hosting, joining and dedicated servers

transport::tcp (length-prefixed frames, never blocking, bounded queues, reads
before writes so a reset cannot eat unread data, graceful close) and
ListenerSet. game_shell: ServerThread (network listener, autosave,
announcements), --host/--join/--autosave, `voxunami serve GAME`. Server::save
saves a running server with its game's state. Tested over real TCP, with real
processes, and from a Windows client to a Linux server. Re

Add Voxunami 2048, the second game

A 4x4x4 board of voxel tiles with a frame and six push plates; left click a
plate to push every tile toward the opposite side, Enter starts a new game.
Rules are plain code on a plain array (board), the server reads the board back
from the world each push, and the score is saved with the world through the new
GameLogic::save_sections. Registered in the launcher as `voxunami 2048`.

creynia/holdumb.readme:
# holdumb

A phone-first web app that teaches **Ultimate Texas Hold'em** from zero to perfect strategy, with an interactive table simulator that shows the EV of every decision before you confirm it.

## Use it

- **Open it:** <https://creynia.github.io/holdumb/>
- **Add to Home screen (Android/Chrome):** open the link, tap the Chrome menu (three dots), then **Add to Home screen** (or **Install app**). It launches full screen and works offline after the first load.
- **Download one offline file:** go to this repo's **Releases**, open **Latest build** and download `holdumb.html` (also linked from the site's Home screen). Open it from Chrome's Downloads list and choose **Chrome**, not "HTML Viewer". It makes no external requests. Progress in this copy is separate from the website copy, so use Settings, then Export/Import to move it.
- **Reload past the cache:** the installed app updates itself and shows "Update available, Reload". If it doesn't, open **Settings, Check for updates**. Tap **Reload** on the toast; if none shows, close the app completely (swipe it away from Recents) and open it again. To wipe the site's data in Chrome on Android: **⋮, Settings, Site settings, All sites, creynia.github.io, Delete & reset**.

### One-time setup (maintainer, from a phone)

The repo must be public (**Settings, General, Danger Zone, Change visibility**). In Chrome on github.com (menu, then **Desktop site** if a tab is hidden):

1. **Settings, Pages, Build and deployment, Source: GitHub Actions.**
2. Run **Deploy to GitHub Pages** from the **Actions** tab (**Run workflow**), or merge to `main`.

If a deploy fails with "deployment in progress", re-run the failed job.

## Is this gambling advice?

No. holdumb is for education. In Ultimate Texas Hold'em the house always has an edge, and no betting system changes that; the lessons show you how big the edge is and which plays cost the least, not how to win. Play money only here. If gambling is causing you or someone you know harm, call **1-800-GAMBLER** (US) or find local resources at your national problem-gambling helpline.

## Development

Requires Node >= 22.12.

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev        # local dev server
npm run check      # lint, typecheck, format check, unit tests
npm run build:all  # dist/ (PWA) and dist-single/holdumb.html
npm run test:e2e   # Playwright (needs a browser, see CONTRIBUTING.md)
```

Design documents are in [`docs/design/`](docs/design/). Planned future work is listed in [`docs/chips.md`](docs/chips.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get involved.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

bradley-benjamin26/GreatBoardgameGetaway.readme:
# Great Boardgame Getaway

A small web app for organizing a boardgame weekend with friends. Everyone adds the games they own or
are bringing, says what they want to play, and schedules play sessions at tables.

Specs and plan live in `specs/001-boardgame-weekend-organizer/`; project rules are in
`.specify/memory/constitution.md`.

## Run it

Requires Node.js 24 or newer.

```sh
npm install
cp .env.example .env     # then edit the values
npm start                # loads settings from the environment, see below
```

`npm start` loads settings from `.env` when the file exists. Values already set in the shell or
process environment take precedence. In hosted environments, provide settings through the host's
environment configuration instead.

Generate a session secret with:

```sh
npm run --silent generate:session-secret
```

Copy the output into `SESSION_SECRET` in `.env` (replacing the placeholder), or into your host's
environment configuration. The command generates 32 cryptographically random bytes as 64 hexadecimal
characters; it does not modify `.env`. Keep the secret private and stable across restarts.

| Setting           | Required | Meaning                                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `EVENT_CODE`      | yes      | Shared code friends enter to create an account. Hand it out outside the app.   |
| `EVENT_DAYS`      | yes      | Comma-separated dates of the event, e.g. `2026-11-06,2026-11-07`.              |
| `SESSION_SECRET`  | yes      | Random string of 32+ characters.                                               |
| `SMTP_URL`        | yes      | Outgoing mail server for password-reset links, e.g. `smtp://user:pw@host:587`. |
| `MAIL_FROM`       | yes      | From address for those emails.                                                 |
| `BASE_URL`        | no       | Public address used in reset links. Default `http://localhost:3000`.           |
| `BGG_TOKEN`       | no       | BoardGameGeek API token. Without it, game search is off; manual entry works.   |
| `DB_PATH`         | no       | SQLite file. Default `./getaway.db`.                                           |
| `PORT`            | no       | Default 3000.                                                                  |
| `COOKIE_INSECURE` | no       | Set to `1` only for local http testing; otherwise cookies are `Secure`.        |

## BoardGameGeek token

BoardGameGeek requires a registered application and a bearer token for its XML API
([Using the XML API](https://boardgamegeek.com/using_the_xml_api)). Approval can take a week or more.
Register at BGG, create a token, and set `BGG_TOKEN`. Read their terms on caching and attribution
before launch; the app shows a "Game data from BoardGameGeek" credit and stores fetched games locally.

## Hosting

- Serve it over HTTPS (a reverse proxy or your host's TLS). Cookies are `Secure`, so sign-in will not
  work over plain http except with `COOKIE_INSECURE=1`.
- The proxy should set `X-Forwarded-For`; sign-in attempts are rate-limited per address.
- Keep the SQLite file on a persistent volume and copy it regularly, e.g. nightly
  (`sqlite3 getaway.db ".backup backup.db"`).
- Prefer a host that publishes its energy mix.

## Test

```sh
npm test            # unit, contract and integration tests
npm run test:e2e    # accessibility, 320 px phone and page-weight checks (needs: npx playwright install chromium)
npm run lint
```

GIider/ringbeat.readme:
# Ringbeat

**Play now:** <https://giider.github.io/ringbeat/>

A browser rhythm game whose charts are generated automatically from RTTTL (Nokia ringtone) text, dressed up as a
late-90s candybar phone: every menu lives on the phone's green LCD, and during a song the note highway runs
right inside that LCD.
All sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API (default voice: a phone piezo buzzer). No dependencies, no build step;
the few assets (pixel font, phone artwork) are made in-repo — see below.

## Screenshots

| Song list | Playing | Playing (compact) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Song list](docs/screenshots/select-desktop.png) | ![Playing](docs/screenshots/play-desktop.png) | ![Playing, compact](docs/screenshots/play-compact.png) |

On narrow screens (under 600 px wide) the phone body is dropped and the LCD fills the window.

Regenerate them with `npm run screenshots` (see below).

## Run

ES modules need an HTTP server (opening `index.html` via `file://` won't work). No dependencies; npm only runs the script:

```
npm start            # http://localhost:8000 (also prints LAN URLs)
npm start -- 9000    # custom port (or PORT=9000 npm start)
npm run dev          # same server, the page reloads whenever a file changes
npm run build        # stage runtime files into dist/ (what CI deploys to GitHub Pages)
npm run bench        # re-measure song difficulty with bots -> src/difficulty.json
npm run screenshots  # regenerate docs/screenshots/*.png from the ?demo= states (Playwright)
npm run font         # rebuild assets/fonts/*.ttf after editing the glyphs in src/pixelfont.js
```

Screenshot states for development: `index.html?demo=play` (also `pause`, `select`, `options`, `info`, `results`,
`settings`) loads the Nokia Tune and freezes a frame at ~10 %.

Versioning: `1.0.<build>` — major.minor from `package.json`, patch = the GitHub Actions run number (stamped by `npm run build` via `BUILD_NUMBER`).
Coverage: `node --test --experimental-test-coverage tests/*.test.mjs`.

Tests: `npm test` (node: core logic, font builder, sprites); `npm run smoke` drives the UI (`tests/smoke.html`) in headless
Chromium via Playwright (`npm install`, then once `npx playwright install chromium`). `tests/rtttl.test.html` and
`tests/smoke.html` also run by hand in a browser (title shows PASS/FAIL).

## Deployment

Every push to `main` runs the tests, builds `dist/` (version `1.0.<run number>`), publishes it as the `latest`
pre-release and deploys it to GitHub Pages ([.github/workflows/deploy.yml](.github/workflows/deploy.yml)).

## Features

Song select with 153 built-in songs (11 full-length) + custom/share links · 3 difficulties · local highscores (top 5 per song/difficulty) ·
full combo / all perfect indicators · timing display · modifiers (speed, mirror, hidden, sudden death, judging; score multiplier) ·
keyboard, touch and gamepad (rebindable) · latency calibration · Nokia-style phone UI with clickable phone keys ·
buzzer or smooth instrument voice.

## Assets

Everything visual is made here, no external fonts or images:

- `src/pixelfont.js` — hand-drawn 5×7 LCD font (ASCII + UI symbols). `scripts/build-font.mjs` compiles it to
  TrueType (`assets/fonts/rb-pixel.ttf` + a bold cut); text is crisp at multiples of 10 px.
- `assets/phone.svg` — the phone shells; the LCD and key hit areas are DOM laid over them.
- `src/pixelart.js` — 1-bit sprites (signal bars, battery, ringing phone, category icons) used as CSS masks.
- `src/cover.js` — per-song 72×28 "picture message" art, generated from the song id.

## Controls

`D F J K` (4 lanes) · `F J K` (easy) · tap lanes on touch · gamepad d-pad/face buttons/shoulders · `Esc` pause · `R` restart.
Menus: arrows, `Enter`, `Esc`/`Backspace`, `O` options — or click the phone's soft keys and keypad.
Full list: [docs/CONTROLS.md](docs/CONTROLS.md). Spec: [docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md). Design: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## RTTTL format notes

rohit267/fpsm.desc: Free, open-source Fraps alternative for Windows: FPS overlay and screenshot hotkey for DX9-DX12 games
rohit267/fpsm.readme:
# fpsm

**A free, open-source Fraps alternative for Windows.** An FPS counter and a screenshot hotkey for
DirectX 9, 10, 11 and 12 games, including newer games that Fraps does not work with.

Fraps hooks old graphics APIs from inside the game, which is why it fails on many newer titles.
fpsm does not touch the game at all: it reads the `Present` events that Windows' DXGI and D3D9
runtimes already publish through ETW (the same source PresentMon uses), so nothing is injected
and there is nothing for anti-cheat to object to.

## Features

- **Lightweight:** one ~4 MB exe, no installer, about 18 MB of RAM while running. It only counts
  frame events, so it adds no load to the game.
- **Open source:** MIT licensed, small readable Go code, no telemetry, no network access.
- **FPS overlay:** a yellow number in a corner of the game, updated twice a second.
- **Screenshots:** press a hotkey to save a PNG of the game. The FPS number is left out of the
  picture, and the number flashes green to confirm the shot.
- **Works with newer games:** DX9 to DX12, no injection into the game.
- **Tray only:** right-click the icon to pick a corner, change the screenshot key, or quit.

## Use

1. Run `fpsm.exe`. It asks for administrator rights once per launch (Windows only lets admins
   read frame events).
2. A yellow "60" icon appears in the tray. Start your game; the frame rate shows in a corner.
3. Press **F10** in the game to take a screenshot. Files go to `Pictures\fpsm`, named like
   `witcher3 2026-10-15 22-30-01.png`.
4. Right-click the tray icon for: Show overlay, Position (four corners), Screenshot key
   (F10, F11, F12, Print Screen or Off), Open screenshots folder, Quit.

Windowed games get the number in the corner of the picture, just under the title bar. Fullscreen
and borderless games get it in the screen corner.

## Supported

- DirectX 9, 10, 11 and 12 games (anything that presents through DXGI or D3D9).
- Screenshots use the Windows Desktop Duplication API, with a plain GDI capture as fallback.
- Tested so far on Windows 11 with The Witcher 3 and GTA: San Andreas.
- Not supported yet: Vulkan and OpenGL games, screenshots on HDR displays.
- True exclusive fullscreen can hide the overlay; borderless and modern fullscreen work.

## Build

Needs Go 1.22 or newer on Windows.

```
go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -H=windowsgui" -o fpsm.exe .
```

Two small command-line helpers:

- `fpsm.exe --probe 8 out.txt` listens for 8 seconds and writes every process that presented
  frames, with its FPS, to `out.txt` (add `--raw` to also list the raw event ids). Useful for
  checking whether a game is detected.
- `fpsm.exe --shot out.png` saves a screenshot of the window in front and exits.

## Roadmap

- Vulkan and OpenGL support.
- HDR screenshots.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

commits.msg:
Initial commit: fpsm, a Fraps alternative for Windows

FPS overlay (corner of the game, 0.5s updates) and a screenshot hotkey for
DX9/10/11/12 games. Frames are counted from DXGI/D3D9 Present ETW events, so
nothing is injected into the game. Screenshots use Desktop Duplication with a
GDI fallback. Tray icon menu: show/hide, corner, screenshot key, quit.

ColeRowellLove/sleeper-fantasy-assistant.desc: Sleeper fantasy football assistant: consensus rankings, waivers, trades, odds and recaps
ColeRowellLove/sleeper-fantasy-assistant.readme:
# Sleeper Fantasy Assistant

[![CI](https://github.com/ColeRowellLove/sleeper-fantasy-assistant/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ColeRowellLove/sleeper-fantasy-assistant/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-blue)
![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/frontend-Next.js-black)
![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)

A public web app that connects to any [Sleeper](https://sleeper.com) fantasy football league by
username, blends several ranking and projection sources into one consensus, and turns it into
waiver alerts, trade ideas, rankings, playoff odds and weekly league recaps.

> **Status:** early development (Milestone 1, foundation). Sleeper's API is public and read-only,
> so the assistant only recommends; you make the move in the Sleeper app.

## What it will do

| Area | Features |
|------|----------|
| Rankings | Consensus positional rankings (weekly and rest of season) with source spread and tiers |
| Waivers | Free-agent scoring, FAAB bid advisor, injury report and status-change alerts |
| Trades | Needs-based trade suggestions, fleece alerts, manager profiles |
| Odds | Monte Carlo season simulator: projected records, playoff, bye and title odds, power rankings |
| Game day | Start/sit optimizer, matchup previews, live win probability, playoff leverage |
| Recaps | Weekly write-ups, trash talk, team names, season awards (family-friendly by default) |
| Offseason | News feed, draft assistant, keeper/dynasty mode, ask-the-assistant chat |

See [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) for the plan, [docs/NEXT_STEPS.md](docs/NEXT_STEPS.md) for what to build next, [docs/TOOLS.md](docs/TOOLS.md) for what each tool and
service is and why it was chosen, [docs/DEPLOY.md](docs/DEPLOY.md) for hosting, and the
[milestones](https://github.com/ColeRowellLove/sleeper-fantasy-assistant/milestones) and
[issues](https://github.com/ColeRowellLove/sleeper-fantasy-assistant/issues) for progress.

## What works today

Connect a league by Sleeper username and the app shows, for each league:

- **Standings:** sortable by any column (rank, team, record, streak, points for and against), with
  each manager's team name and your own team highlighted, plus the playoff line.
- **Rosters:** starters, bench, injured reserve and taxi, with injury status and each player's NFL
  game (kickoff in your time zone, live, final, or bye week).
- **Lineups:** every matchup side by side for any week, in the Sleeper starter order.
- **Players:** every relevant NFL player through your league: filter by position and availability, search, and sort by Sleeper adds and drops, positional rank, season points under your scoring, and projected points.
- **Player pop-up:** click any player (rosters, lineups, Players tab) for their bio, position rank, week-by-week points with every stat that counted, this week's projected stats, and past seasons, all scored with your league's rules.
- **Projections:** projected points (scored with your league's own rules) next to actual points on rosters and lineups, with a team total in each matchup.
- **Settings:** the league's rules and scoring as Sleeper reports them.

Dark and light themes, phone and desktop layouts, and keyboard and screen-reader support throughout.
Kickoff times come from [nflverse](https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data) (CC BY 4.0).

## Principles

1. **Consensus over any single source**: every value shows its source spread.
2. **Calibrated numbers**: odds come from simulation, with accuracy tracked against reality.
3. **League-aware**: scoring, roster slots and deadlines are read from Sleeper, never hard-coded.
4. **Explain every recommendation**: a one-line why plus the numbers behind it.

## Architecture

A Python core ingests data on a schedule into Postgres; the web app only reads from it.

```
Sleeper API + other sources -> ingest jobs -> Postgres -> FastAPI -> Next.js dashboard
                                   |

janroudaut/kaboom-arena.desc: Kaboom Arena: a fan-made retro bomb arena game for the browser (solo, local, online, 3D)
janroudaut/kaboom-arena.readme:
# 💣 Kaboom Arena A free retro arcade arena that runs in your browser: drop bombs, blast walls, grab power-ups and outlast your rivals. Solo against bots, local on one screen, or online with a room code. Works on desktop, phone and tablet, installable as a PWA, solo mode works offline. **💣 Play it: https://kaboom.philament.club** > A fan-made tribute to Konami's Bomberman. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Konami. > All graphics are drawn in code, no original assets are used.

## Features - **Modes**: solo vs 1-3 bots, local 2-4 players (keyboards and gamepads), online up to 4 players with a 4-letter room code. Best of 3 rounds, sudden death after 90 s. - **Rules**: grid arena, chain-reacting bombs, destructible walls, power-ups (extra bomb, range, speed). - **Bots** that dodge blasts (with chain reactions), pick up bonuses and hunt walls and rivals. - **Three looks**: Classic pixel art (2D canvas), 3D (Three.js), and **DLSS 5**, a deliberately over-the-top parody: bloom, chromatic aberration, "Neural Faces", fake frame generation counter, and a very real dynamic resolution. - **Every device**: keyboard, gamepad (Gamepad API), touch (virtual joystick), pause with `P`/`Esc`/Start. - **PWA**: installable, offline solo, network-first service worker. - **Smooth online play**: client-side prediction, snapshot interpolation, compact snapshots, RTT badge. ## Controls | | Move | Bomb | |---|---|---| | Player 1 | `W A S D` / `Z Q S D` | `Space` | | Player 2 | Arrow keys | `Enter` | | Gamepad | D-pad / left stick | A / B / X / Y | | Touch | Joystick | 💣 button | Pause: `P`, `Esc`, ⏸ button or gamepad Start (solo and local only). Append `?lag=120&jitter=40` to the URL to simulate a bad network. ## Run it locally **You don't need Ruby or Rails to play.** Solo, local multiplayer, the bots and the 3D modes are **plain static files**: no build step, no database, nothing to install beyond a static file server pointed at `public/`. Pick whatever you already have: ```sh python3 -m http.server 8000 -d public # Python 3 (macOS, Linux, Windows) npx serve public # Node.js php -S localhost:8000 -t public # PHP ruby -run -e httpd public -p 8000 # Ruby, no gem needed deno run -A jsr:@std/http/file-server public # Deno busybox httpd -f -p 8000 -h public # BusyBox ``` Then open http://localhost:8000. (Use `localhost`, browsers only enable the service worker and the Gamepad API on secure origins; any other host needs HTTPS.) **Ruby/Rails is only needed for the online mode** (a small WebSocket relay, Ruby 3.4+, no database): ```sh bundle install bin/rails s -b 0.0.0.0 # http://localhost:3117, also serves the game ``` Without it, everything else works; only the "Create a room" / "Join" buttons won't connect. Tests (Node 20+, no dependencies): ```sh cd public/game && node --test sim.test.mjs ai.test.mjs netcode.test.mjs ``` ## How it works - `public/game/sim.js` is the whole game: a pure, deterministic 60 Hz simulation. - **Solo/local**: the browser runs the simulation and the bots (`ai.js`). - **Online**: the host's browser runs the simulation and broadcasts snapshots; guests send inputs and predict their own player (`netcode.js`). Rails/ActionCable (`app/channels/room_channel.rb`) is a dumb, hardened relay: server-assigned host, message allow-list per role, size and rate limits, per-IP connection caps. The host is tru

# SFoEv1
Simple bullet hell game created in an hour

## Leaderboard setup (Firebase + Vercel)
Scores are stored only in Firebase Firestore.
1. Firebase console: create a project, add a Web app, enable **Firestore** and **Authentication -> Anonymous**.
2. Paste the web app config into `firebase-config.js`.
3. Publish `firestore.rules` (Firestore -> Rules).
4. Deploy on Vercel. No environment variables are needed for Firebase.

Only the top 50 players (one entry per username) are kept; entries pushed out are deleted from Firestore.

swulis00-crypto/library-game.readme:
# 📚 책길 탐험대 (v2) — 게임으로 배우는 도서관 책 찾기

> 🌐 바로 하기: https://swulis00-crypto.github.io/library-game/
>
> 미로 · 책꽂이 정리 · 외계인 · 벽돌 깨기 · 뱀 · 두더지!
> 고전게임 6가지로 **도서관 청구기호(KDC 제6판 + 이재철 저자기호)** 와 **책꽂이 순서 규칙**을 익히는 어린이용 웹 게임

---

## 🔒 개인정보 원칙

- 이름·별명 입력 없음, 순위표 없음.
- 브라우저(localStorage)에 남는 것은 **사서 선생님이 등록한 도서/문제 데이터**와 **소리 켬/꺼짐 설정**만입니다.
- 캐릭터(아바타), 이번 시간에 모은 별, 점수는 모두 메모리에만 있고 새로고침하면 사라집니다.
- 예전 버전이 남긴 이용자/점수 데이터가 있으면 첫 실행 때 자동으로 삭제합니다.

---

## 🎮 게임 6종

| 게임 | 원작 | 배우는 것 | 재미 요소 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🧭 **미로 탈출** | 팩맨 | 주제 → 분류번호 찾기 | 별 조각 모으기, 먼지 도깨비 피하기, 출구 화살표, 20초 후 힌트 반짝임 |
| 📚 **책꽂이 정리** | 정렬 퍼즐 | 분류번호 → 저자기호 가나다 → 1권·2권 순서 | 드래그/탭 두 가지 조작, 칸마다 ✓✗ 즉시 표시, 3번 틀리면 정답 공개 |
| 👾 **외계인 격퇴** | 스페이스 인베이더 | 주제별 분류번호 빨리 찾기 | 모든 외계인이 같은 색(번호를 읽어야 함), 콤보, 도전 모드 폭탄 |
| 🧱 **벽돌 깨기** | 알카노이드 | 000~900 백 자리 구별 | 미션 벽돌은 1타, 나머지는 2타. 틀린 벽돌을 치면 "이 번호는 ○○" 알려줌 |
| 🐍 **책벌레 뱀** | 스네이크 | 청구기호 오름차순 | 다음 목표 반짝임, 먹을수록 몸 길어짐, 워프 이동, 스와이프 조작 |
| 🔨 **두더지 팡팡** | 두더지 잡기 | 저자기호 읽기, 순발력 | 세 번에 한 번은 정답 두더지 보장, 콤보, 뿅망치 커서 |

### 공통 재미 장치
- **3·2·1·출발!** 카운트다운과 조작법 안내
- **콤보**: 연속 정답마다 보너스 점수(최대 +100)와 효과음
- **스테이지 클리어 카드**: 정답과 "왜 그런지" 설명을 바로 보여주고 다음 문제로
- **힌트 토스트**: 틀리면 즉시 짧은 힌트가 화면 위에 뜸(게임은 계속)
- **별점(⭐ 최대 3개)** + 꽃가루 + 북이의 배움 카드(틀린 문제 다시 보기)
- **내 캐릭터**: 8가지 동물 중 선택 → 미로의 탐험가, 뱀 머리, 우주선 조종사, 막대로 등장
- **매번 다른 문제**: 등록 문제 일부 + KDC 분류표/도서 목록으로 자동 생성한 문제를 섞어 출제

---

## 📖 학습 내용

### KDC 제6판 10가지 큰 숫자
`000 총류` `100 철학` `200 종교` `300 사회과학` `400 순수과학` `500 기술과학` `600 예술` `700 언어` `800 문학` `900 역사`

### 이재철 저자기호
성(김) + 이름 번호(68) + 책 제목 첫 글자의 첫소리(ㅂ) → `김68ㅂ`

### 책꽂이 순서 5가지 규칙
1. 왼쪽 → 오른쪽, 위 칸 → 아래 칸
2. 분류번호 작은 것부터
3. 소수점은 한 자리씩 비교 (813.6 < 813.62 < 813.7)
4. 번호가 같으면 저자기호 가나다순
5. 1권 → 2권, c.1 → c.2

---

## ⚙️ 사서 선생님 화면

상단 메뉴 **사서 선생님** → 숫자 4자리 (기본 `1234`, [adminPanelScreen.js](src/components/adminPanelScreen.js)의 `checkPin` 에서 변경)

- **도서 자료 관리**: 우리 도서관 책 등록/삭제, 기본 16권 복원
  - 등록한 책은 미로(힌트), 책꽂이 정리(정렬), 두더지(저자기호) 문제로 자동 출제됩니다.
- **문제 검토**: 게임별 등록 문제 수 확인, 초기화
- **백업 & 복원**: 도서·문제 데이터를 JSON으로 내보내기/가져오기 (학생 정보 없음)

---

## 💻 실행

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm run build    # dist/ 생성
```

- PC: 방향키/WASD, 스페이스바, 마우스
- 태블릿/휴대폰: 화면 터치 패드, 스와이프, 탭 (화면 아래 메뉴 바)

링크 미리보기용 이미지는 [design/og-image.html](design/og-image.html)을 1200×630으로 렌더링한 `public/og-image.png`입니다.

```

jasonuithol/Ultima5Revolutions.readme:
# Ultima V Revolutions — a Rust decompilation of Ultima V (PC, 1988)

A faithful Rust port of the DOS *Ultima V: Warriors of Destiny* engine, produced by decompiling the
original executable and its 23 overlays (Ghidra) and translating every function. The port contains
game LOGIC only: all text, maps, graphics, fonts and saves are read at run time from your own copy of
the game (the GOG release), which is never modified except for the save files the game writes itself
(SAVED.GAM, *.OOL), exactly like the original.

## Running

    source ~/.local/opt/u5env.sh          # Rust toolchain (rustup) on PATH
    cd rust && cargo build --release
    U5_DIR="/path/to/Ultima 5" ./target/release/ultima5   # your own (GOG) copy of the game

Environment variables:
- `U5_DIR=/path/to/game`  game directory (the original DOS files: ULTIMA.EXE, *.OVL, *.DAT, *.16, …)
- `U5_VIDEO=E|C|T|H`      video driver flavour as the original's command-line letter (default E = EGA)
- `U5_HEADLESS=1`         no window (for scripted tests), with
  `U5_KEYS="ms:KEY,ms:KEY,..."` scripted keys (chars, ENTER, ESC, SPACE, UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT, F1..),
  `U5_EXIT_MS=n` exit after n ms, `U5_SHOT=file.ppm` screenshot at exit (plus _1.._3 quarter shots)
- `U5_TRACE_KEYS=1`       log every key the game reads
- `U5_CPU_SPEED=n`        CPU speed factor used for busy-wait delays and speaker effects (default 2200 ≈ the GOG DOSBox profile; larger = faster)

Window: 320x200 EGA framebuffer scaled 3x. Keys are the original's: letters for commands, arrows or
keypad for movement, Enter/Space/Esc in menus. Sound is the PC speaker emulated through PipeWire
(`pw-play`), falling back to `paplay`/`aplay`.

## Layout

- `rust/src/engine/`  the ROOT module of ULTIMA.EXE (gfx wrappers, text windows, input, files,
  utilities, effects, and `rest.rs` with the rest of the engine incl. `main_entry`).
- `rust/src/ovl/`     one module per overlay (town, mainout, dungeon, combat, cast, talk, shoppes, ...).
- `rust/src/platform/` framebuffer window (minifb), EGA.DRV reimplementation (`video.rs`), keyboard,
  timer, speaker.
- `rust/src/mem.rs`, `loader.rs`, `g.rs`  emulated memory (DGROUP at its original address, overlay
  tables at theirs), file loader, generated global-offset constants.
- `analysis/`  the reverse-engineering record: ARCHITECTURE.md, per-function records (`*.jsonl`),
  per-module overviews (`*.md`), driver API, symbol table, translation briefs.
- `ghidra/scripts/` + `ghidra/run_*.sh` the Ghidra pipeline; its outputs (`ghidra/export`, `decomp/`,
  `decomp_named/`) are derived from the original binaries and are not part of the repository —
  run the pipeline against your own copy to regenerate them (see analysis/ARCHITECTURE.md).
- `tools/`  merge/symbol/stub generators and the DOSBox comparison harness (`tools/dosbox/`).

## Requirements and legal note

You need your own copy of the original PC game (e.g. the GOG release). This repository holds a
reimplementation of the program logic and the notes made while reverse-engineering it; it contains
no game data, text, graphics or binaries. Ultima V is a trademark/copyright of its owners.

## Conventions worth knowing

- Rust parameter order equals the Ghidra decompiled order, which is the REVERSE of the original source
  order (the game was compiled with the Pascal convention). Doc comments give the original address.
- Near pointers are `u16` DGROUP offsets, far pointers `u32` linear addresses; globals go through
  `gm.g8/g16/set_g8/...` with constants from `g.rs`.
- `// TODO(verify):` marks places where the original relied on uninitialised data or where the
  decompilation was ambiguous; behaviour was translated literally.

hazanaya/scipaper-puzzle.readme:
# SciPaper Puzzle

A web game that cuts a scientific paper into index cards, asks you to reassemble it, and then makes you write the ending yourself before revealing what the authors actually concluded.

It is a digital version of a grad-school exercise: print a paper, cut every section into slips, remove the Results and Discussion, and make students rebuild the argument and predict the ending before they see it.

## Status

Live at **https://hazanaya.github.io/scipaper-puzzle/** (deployed from `main` by GitHub Actions). Early, playable. The full loop works offline: import (paste, PDF, or bundled demo), reassemble the cards, write the withheld sections, compare against the authors with a concept-coverage meter. Not yet playtested with real papers from the lab.

## Quick start

Requires Node 20 or newer.

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open the URL Vite prints (usually http://localhost:5173). Pick **Demo paper** on the first screen to play immediately.

Other commands:

```
npm test          # unit tests for the parser, card cutter, scorer, coverage meter
npm run build     # type-check and build a static site into dist/
npm run preview   # serve the built site locally
```

The build in `dist/` is plain static files. Host it anywhere, or open it from any subpath.

## How to play

1. **Import.** Paste the text of a paper (headings included), drop in a PDF, or load the demo. Check the detected sections; fix a role, skip a section, or change which sections are withheld.
2. **Reassemble.** The abstract, introduction, and methods arrive as a shuffled deck of index cards. Drag them into the section slots, or click a card and then a slot. Press **Check** to score. Hints move one card for a point.
3. **Write the ending.** The results, discussion, and conclusion are hidden. Write your own version of each from what you assembled.
4. **Compare.** Read your version beside the authors'. The coverage strip shows which of their key terms you used and which you missed. Copy a Markdown summary, replay with a new shuffle or harder difficulty, or import another paper.

Progress is saved in the browser, so a refresh resumes where you were.

## Sharing it

The build is a static site, so it can live on any static host. The repo ships a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`) that tests, builds, and deploys to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`.

**First-time GitHub Pages setup**

Already done for this repo: it lives at github.com/hazanaya/scipaper-puzzle with Pages set to deploy from the workflow, so every push to `main` redeploys https://hazanaya.github.io/scipaper-puzzle/. For a fresh fork: push to GitHub (free Pages needs a public repo), set Settings → Pages source to **GitHub Actions** (or `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages -f build_type=workflow`), then push to `main`.

**Putting it on hazaelanaya.com (Squarespace)**

Squarespace cannot host the app's files directly, but it can be the front door:

- *Own subdomain (cleanest).* In Squarespace → Domains → DNS, add a CNAME record for `puzzle` pointing to `hazanaya.github.io`. Then add a file `public/CNAME` containing `puzzle.hazaelanaya.com`, commit, and set that custom domain in the repo's Pages settings. The app then runs at `https://puzzle.hazaelanaya.com`.
- *Embedded page.* Add a page on the site with a Code block containing `<iframe src="https://hazanaya.github.io/scipaper-puzzle/" style="width:100%;height:90vh;border:0"></iframe>`. Custom code blocks need the Business plan or higher.
- *Plain link.* Add a page or button that links to the Pages URL. Works on any plan.

## Project layout

```
.
├── README.md            # This file
├── AGENTS.md            # Instructions for AI coding tools
├── CLAUDE.md            # Stub pointing AI tools to AGENTS.md
├── DESIGN.md            # Game design: loop, phases, scoring, goals, non-goals
├── HANDOFF.md           # Current state and next steps
├── CHANGELOG.md         # Notable changes
├── LICENSE
├── docs/
│   ├

DanDanKM/remis-bubble-club.readme:
# Remi's Bubble Club

A counting, letters, spelling, music and talking-to-a-bee game for Remi, hosted by Irie the sloth, Katy, Gaga, HUNTR/X, Uncle Archie and Bumble the Bee.

- `index.html` is the whole game. Open it, or visit the GitHub Pages address for this repository.
- `voices/` holds optional recorded character voices. Without it the game uses the device's built-in voices.
- `make_voices.py` records every line the game speaks with ElevenLabs and fills `voices/`.

## Playing on the iPad

Open the Pages address in Safari, tap Share, then "Add to Home Screen". The first tap unlocks sound.
Singing in tune and the roar meter use the microphone. Safari asks once; allow it.

Buzz Garden (Bumble the Bee) listens for Remi's voice: she says a letter, or her name, and Bumble flies to the flower.
The first listen in each visit starts from the big "Say it" button (Safari asks once for speech recognition); after that Bumble
listens by herself after each question. Tapping the flowers always works too, so the game never depends on the microphone.
If the home-screen icon does not listen, open the same address in Safari itself.

## Adding real character voices

1. Make a free account at elevenlabs.io and copy your API key (profile menu, API keys).
2. On a computer with Python 3, open a terminal in this folder and set the key:
   - PowerShell: `$env:ELEVENLABS_API_KEY = "your key"`
   - Mac: `export ELEVENLABS_API_KEY="your key"`
3. `python make_voices.py --list` shows every line and the credit cost. `python make_voices.py --voices` lists the voices on your account; paste any you prefer into `VOICE_IDS` at the top of the script.
4. `python make_voices.py` records the lines into `voices/` and writes `voices/manifest.json`. It only records what is missing, so it is safe to re-run.
5. Commit and push the `voices` folder (or upload it next to `index.html`). Reload the game. The grown-ups panel (hold the gear) shows how many clips were found and lists any line still spoken by the device voice.

To name your Country in Uncle Archie's Acknowledgement, type it in the grown-ups panel and record that line with `python make_voices.py --country Wurundjeri` (use your Country's name).

## Changing voices later

Delete that character's folder inside `voices/`, change its id in `VOICE_IDS`, and run the script again.

noamk15/the-last-exit.readme:
# THE LAST EXIT

A first-person horror maze that runs entirely in the browser.
Three glowing keys are hidden in a dark maze. Find them, unlock the exit, get out.

**Play:** https://noamk15.github.io/the-last-exit/

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `W A S D` / arrows (`Z Q S D` also work) | move |
| mouse | look (click "Enter the maze" to lock the pointer) |
| `Esc` / `P` | pause |
| `M` | mute / unmute |

## Run locally

Module imports do not work from `file://`, so serve the folder:

```
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

then open http://localhost:8000/

## Useful URL parameters

- `?seed=266` : fixed maze layout (any number or word). Good short layouts for a demo: `266`, `288`, `30`.
- `?autostart=1` : skip the menu (used for automated screenshots).

## Tech

- Plain HTML / CSS / JavaScript modules, no build step, no backend.
- [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) 0.186, vendored in `vendor/` (works offline).
- Maze: recursive backtracker on a 13x13 grid with a few extra loops, seeded PRNG, BFS to guarantee keys and exit are reachable.
- Textures and sounds are generated procedurally (canvas + Web Audio API). No external assets.

## Before each deploy

```
node scripts/bump.mjs      # stamps ?v= on imports so browsers do not serve stale JS
node scripts/e2e.mjs       # end-to-end smoke test in headless Chrome
```

## Verify the maze generator

```
node scripts/check-maze.mjs 1000
```

## Layout

```
index.html         overlays (start / HUD / pause / victory) + import map
css/style.css      cinematic UI
js/main.js         Three.js scene, game loop, state machine
js/maze.js         generation, BFS, key / exit placement
js/player.js       movement + circle-vs-grid collisions
js/ui.js           DOM helpers, timer, best time (localStorage)
js/audio.js        procedural drone, footsteps, chimes
vendor/            three.module.js + three.core.js (MIT)
```

DeAnthonee/Liargame.readme:
# Chameleon

A mobile web version of the party game *The Chameleon*. Every player joins a
lobby from their own phone using a 4-letter room code. 3 to 8 players.

## How a game works

1. One player opens the site, enters a name and taps **Create a room**. They
   become the host and get a room code to share.
2. Everyone else opens the site on their phone, enters their name and the code.
3. The host picks options (scoring, debate timer, topic cards) and starts.
4. Each round, every phone shows the Topic Card. Everyone except the Chameleon
   also sees the Secret Word highlighted.
5. Starting with the dealer, players take turns saying one related word out
   loud and tapping once to pass the turn. The host can skip straight to the
   discussion if someone's phone is closed.
6. Debate (optional timer), then everyone votes secretly on their own phone.
   Ties go to the dealer.
7. If the accused is the Chameleon, they get one guess at the Secret Word
   (two guesses in a 3-player game). Official scoring applies: first to 5 wins.

Players who close their phone keep their seat for 10 minutes and rejoin
automatically when they reopen the page. Rooms close after 2 hours of
inactivity or 15 minutes with nobody connected.

## Running locally

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

Then open http://localhost:3000. To test with phones on the same Wi-Fi, open
`http://<your-computer-ip>:3000` on each phone. Run `npm test` to run the test suite.

## Deployment notes (for whoever hosts it)

- **Runtime:** Node.js 18 or newer (tested on 22 and 26). No database, no build step.
- **Install:** `npm ci` (uses the committed `package-lock.json`). Only `socket.io-client` is a devDependency, and it is needed for `npm test` only.
- **Test gate:** `npm test` (syntax checks plus `node:test` suites). Tests bind random ports on 127.0.0.1 only.
- **Start:** `node server.js` from the repo root. Reads `PORT` (default 3000) and `HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`).
- **Optional env:** `DATA_DIR=/path/outside/the/clone` makes the server snapshot live rooms to `DATA_DIR/rooms.json` on SIGTERM and restore them on the next boot, so a redeploy mid-game is a few-second blip instead of a lost game. Without it, rooms live in memory only and a restart closes them. `BUILD_ID` overrides the build identifier reported by `/healthz` (otherwise the git commit is used).
- **Health:** `GET /healthz` returns `{"ok":true,"version":"1.4.0","build":"<git sha>","playing":<live matches>,"rooms":<n>,"players":<connected>,"uptime":<s>,"draining":<bool>}`.
- **Shutdown:** SIGTERM or SIGINT drains cleanly, normally in about a second, worst case 10 seconds.
- **WebSockets:** Socket.IO on the same port, path `/socket.io/`. The reverse proxy or tunnel must pass WebSocket upgrades through. The client derives `ws`/`wss` from the page URL; nothing is hardcoded.
- **Caching:** `index.html` is served with `no-store`. CSS and JS are referenced as `/a/<content-hash>/…` and served with `max-age=31536000, immutable`, so every deploy gets fresh URLs. Unhashed paths such as `/js/client.js` are served with `no-cache`.
- **Single instance:** game state lives in memory. Run exactly one process.
- **External services:** none. The server serves the Socket.IO client itself; fonts are system fonts.

## Topic cards

Built-in cards live in `public/js/topics.js` as 4x4 grids of 16 words. Add a
card by appending an object with a `name` and 16 `words`. The host can also
create custom cards from the lobby; those live for the life of the room.

## Files

- `server.js` – Express + Socket.IO game server (rooms, rounds, scoring)
- `public/index.html` – app shell
- `public/css/styles.css` – mobile-first styling
- `public/js/client.js` – phone client (lobby and all game screens)
- `public/js/topics.js` – topic card data, shared by server and client

# Matcha Café Empire

Idle-/Tycoon-Browserspiel: Baue ein kleines Matcha-Café in Berlin zur Kette bis nach Bali aus. Gäste bestellen an der Theke, Baristas bereiten zu, Bedienungen servieren, Putzkräfte halten alles sauber – du kaufst Ausstattung, stellst Personal ein, behebst den Engpass, pflegst die Zufriedenheit, eröffnest Standorte und sammelst per Franchise-Reset Zen. Läuft im Browser und als installierbare PWA, auf Deutsch und Englisch, ohne Werbung und ohne Käufe; der Spielstand bleibt lokal im Browser.

Version 1.0.0 – Änderungen in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

| Handy                                                         | Desktop                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ![Café auf dem Handy (DE)](docs/screenshots/v1/mobile-de.png) | ![Café auf dem Desktop (EN)](docs/screenshots/v1/desktop-en.png) |

Weitere Screenshots: [`docs/screenshots/v1/`](docs/screenshots/v1/); Phase 2 (bedientes Café, Pipeline-Karte): [`docs/screenshots/s10/`](docs/screenshots/s10/); Ausstattung in fünf Optik-Stufen (Katalog, Café am Start / in der Mitte / im Luxus-Ausbau): [`docs/screenshots/ausstattung/`](docs/screenshots/ausstattung/).

## Technik

Vite + TypeScript + Phaser 3 (Szene), DOM-Overlay für die UI, i18n DE/EN, Spielstand in `localStorage` mit Sicherungen in IndexedDB. Die Spiellogik in `src/core` ist pur und ohne Phaser/DOM getestet; Einnahmen kommen nur aus dem Rate-Modell, die Figuren in der Szene sind Kosmetik.

## Start

```
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # http://localhost:5173/Tycoon-/  (?lang=de|en, ?tutorial=0 ohne Tutorial)
pnpm check        # lint + typecheck + test
pnpm e2e          # Playwright (einmalig: pnpm exec playwright install chromium)
pnpm build        # Produktions-Build nach dist/ (base: /Tycoon-/)
pnpm preview      # Build lokal ansehen
pnpm sim --hours 4  # Headless-Balancing-Simulation (--set spawn.base=0.17 --staffGrowth 1.7 für Experimente)
pnpm art            # Sprites neu rendern (braucht Chromium: PW_CHROMIUM=…)
```

Deploy: Der Build in `dist/` ist statisch und läuft unter jedem Pfad `/Tycoon-/`, z. B. GitHub Pages (Workflow `pages.yml`).

## Doku

- `CLAUDE.md` – Projektregeln
- `docs/PLAN.md` – Architektur und Session-Plan (S0–S9, Phase 2: S10–S12)
- `docs/GAME_DESIGN.md` – Spieldesign und Formeln
- `docs/UI_STYLE.md` – UI- und Grafikstil
- `docs/STATUS.md` – Stand, offene Punkte, Entscheidungen, Balancing-Snapshot
- `docs/ROUTINE.md` – autonomer Session-Loop
- `docs/ASSETS.md` – Herkunft/Lizenz aller Assets

# Space Invaders Game

A classic Space Invaders game implemented in HTML5 canvas and JavaScript with SVG-based sprites, served by a Laravel application.

## Features
- Pixel-art sprites: three invader types (30/20/10 points) with two-frame animation, a mystery UFO worth 50–300, and a classic green cannon
- Fleet marches in steps and speeds up as it thins; each wave starts faster and lower
- Invaders fire back, with destructible bunkers to hide behind
- **Boss every fifth wave**: a large saucer with a health bar that sweeps the top of the screen firing three-way volleys
- **Power-ups** dropped by dying invaders: Rapid fire (R), Spread shot (S), Shield (H), extra life (L)
- **Combo multiplier** up to x4 for consecutive hits; missing a shot resets it
- Three lives, bonus life every 1,500 points (max 5), respawn invincibility, wave bonus
- Score popups, particle explosions, screen shake, CRT scanlines

# Tower Stacker

The first mobile game of Gaming Company's Mobile Studio (Murat and Kerem). Blocks slide across the screen; tap to drop one on the tower. The overhang is cut off, so every miss makes the next block narrower, until it is too thin to land. One thumb, portrait, sessions under three minutes.

## Open the project (Kerem's Mac, Unity 6.6)

1. Clone this repository, or download it as a zip and unzip it.
2. In Unity Hub, under Installs, install **Unity 6000.6.6f1** (Unity 6.6) with the **iOS Build Support** module. Then click **Add** and choose the `tower-stacker` folder. The project is pinned to 6000.6.6f1; if Hub offers a newer 6.6 patch, accept the upgrade.
3. Open the project. Unity creates the `Library` folder on first open; this takes a few minutes.
4. Open any scene (File > New Scene is fine) and press **Play**. The game builds itself from code, so there is no scene to set up.
5. For the phone preview: Edit > Project Settings > Player, set the default orientation to Portrait, then in the Game view choose a portrait resolution such as 1080x1920.

If Unity complains that `Input` is not available, go to Edit > Project Settings > Player > Other Settings > Active Input Handling and choose **Both**.

## How the code is organised

| File | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `Assets/Scripts/Bootstrap.cs` | Creates the camera and the game objects when the app starts. |
| `Assets/Scripts/StackManager.cs` | The whole core loop: sliding block, tap to drop, cutting the overhang, score, game over, restart. The numbers under `Tuning` are the ones to play with. |
| `Assets/Scripts/Block.cs` | One block, drawn as a floor of a Bosphorus house: shaded edge, cornice with dentils, framed windows with sills that light up at night; also how a cut-off piece falls away. |
| `Assets/Scripts/BosphorusScenery.cs` | The theme: sky from morning to night, sun, moon, stars, clouds, the Istanbul skyline with its lights and their reflection, the sea, the quay, a ferry with smoke and a wake, and seagulls. |
| `Assets/Scripts/BosphorusArt.cs` | The artwork itself: the skyline in two depths (Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia, Galata, Maiden's Tower, the Bosphorus Bridge, houses, trees), the ferry, the gull, clouds, sun, moon and quay, painted at start. |
| `Assets/Scripts/PixelCanvas.cs` | A small painter that draws shapes into pixels and makes a sprite, so there are still no image files in the project. |
| `Assets/Scripts/Effects.cs` | Camera shake and the sounds (drops, perfects, ferry horn, seagulls). All generated in code, so there are no audio files yet. |
| `Assets/Scripts/Flash.cs` | The white flash that grows and fades on a perfect drop. |
| `Assets/Scripts/GameUI.cs` | Score and prompts on screen. Temporary; replaced by a real UI in week 2. |

## Plan

The two-week plan lives in the Studio Blueprint doc (Tower Stacker tab). Short version: week 1 is making the loop feel good on a phone, week 2 is a real UI, sound, and the first build on an iPhone.

nikniq/nq-towers.readme:
# NQ Towers

A small canvas tower-defence game served by Laravel.

## Layout

- `public_html/` is the web root (instead of Laravel's default `public/`). Point your web server's document root here. The override lives in `bootstrap/app.php` (`usePublicPath`).
- `public_html/game.js`, `favicon.svg`, `ads.txt`, `assets/` are the static game files.
- `resources/views/game.blade.php` is the page; `app/Http/Controllers/GameController.php` renders it.
- `config/game.php` holds the cache-busting build token (`GAME_BUILD`) and the Google Analytics ID (`GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`), both read from `.env`.
- `scripts/generate_sounds.py` generates the WAV files in `public_html/assets/`.

## Setup

```sh
composer install
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
php artisan serve
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000.
