LouisMareau/battle-frontier.readme:
# Battle Frontier

An original creature-catching RPG and its engine, in Rust: one program for the browser
(WebAssembly, on WebGPU or WebGL 2) and for the desktop, holding both the game and the
tools to build it (a content browser and a map editor so far). "Battle Frontier" is a
working name. Battles are its own: timed hits and blocks on a classic RPG menu, MP, moves
that level up and change shape, locks on big attacks, rounds ordered by Speed, battles that
grow up to 6v6, staged in 3D on the overworld map, day and night.

Everything the game is made of is data, in `content/`. Until it has its own creatures and
moves, the author develops with local placeholders in `temporary/`, a space that is never
committed (see below): without them the game has no battles yet, and the editors work.

## Running it

Needs Rust (stable, with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target), [Trunk](https://trunkrs.dev)
for the web build, Node 22+ and a Chrome for the checks. Build output goes to `build/` (set in `.cargo/config.toml`, with 8 parallel jobs).

```bash
cargo run -p engine-content --bin content -- check   # what's in content/ and temporary/, every broken reference
cargo test -p engine-core              # the battle rules on their own fixtures: 15 tests, incl. 60 simulated battles and every mechanic
cargo test -p engine-world             # maps: records round-trip, tree areas
cargo run -p engine-game --release     # the desktop game (run from this folder, or set GAME_ROOT)
cargo run -p engine-game --release -- --explore [ID]   # straight into the overworld (the saved map, or ID)
trunk build --release                  # the site in build/dist/ (content/ only, never temporary/)
node tools/serve.mjs                   # serves the site at http://localhost:8080, with temporary/ next to it
node tools/check.mjs [seconds=60]      # plays battles in a headless Chrome (needs creatures and encounters), frame times -> screenshots/
node tools/frames.mjs [encounter]      # frame times of one encounter, second by second
node tools/perf.mjs [tile=4] [size=3840x2160]   # how fast it draws, uncapped: menu, map views, editing, walking, a battle
node tools/mapcheck.mjs [map=ID]       # drives the map editor (paint, levels, props, trees, undo, download)
node tools/buildcheck.mjs              # drives the Build tool (footprint, doors, floors, confirm, walk in, turn, move)
node tools/zonecheck.mjs               # creatures roaming, the debug view, a zone painted and linked to a treeline
node tools/assetcheck.mjs              # the asset browser: folders, a row dragged, a .glb dropped in, unstackable, saves
node tools/worldcheck.mjs              # the World view: a piece dragged into place, the world saved, a walk across a seam into a chunked map
cargo run -p engine-content --bin content -- chunk MAP    # a map stored as chunk files (unchunk: rows again)
cargo run -p engine-world --bin export-glb -- map test_meadow   # a map (or prop ID, props, building MAP ID) as .glb for Blender
node tools/shot.mjs "map:test_meadow"  # one screenshot of a state, from commands
```

The desktop build takes `--preset ID` (start that encounter), `--auto` (the AI plays your
side), `--time morning|day|night`, `--levels 1-5` (every move at that level), `--maps [ID]` (the
map editor), `--exit-after SECONDS`, `--stats` (frames per second, the worst frame
gap and the time each frame keeps the processor busy, printed every second) and `--no-vsync`
(draws as fast as it can, not at the screen's rate: with `--stats`, what the machine could
do). The browser build takes the same as
`<body data-cmd="start:ID;auto:1">` (also `editor`, `maps`, `map:ID`, `back`, `scale:50-100`
and `shadows:off|low|medium|high`) and
writes `data-state`, `data-round`, `data-fps`, `data-maxgap`, `data-cpu`, `data-cpupeak`,
`data-draws`, `data-tris`, `data-shadowtris`, `data-culled`, `data-pending` (the timing
read in progress), and in the map editor `data-map`, `data-mapsize`, `data-tool`, `data-level`,
`data-props`, `data

gladimdim/super-desktop-tictactoe.desc: A tic-tac-toe card on the SUPER DESKTOP desktop: play the computer or a friend. Comes back open or closed as you left it.
gladimdim/super-desktop-tictactoe.readme:
# TicTacToe for SUPER DESKTOP

A simple tic-tac-toe game on a card on the
[SUPER DESKTOP](https://github.com/gladimdim/super-desktop) desktop: a big
board and the score beside it. Play the computer or a friend.

| Your turn | The computer wins | Two players, a draw |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![A game in progress](docs/game.png) | ![The computer's winning line highlighted](docs/win.png) | ![A full board in two-player mode](docs/duo.png) |

## Use it

- **Click a square** to play. Against the computer you are X; in
  **2 Players** mode X and O take turns at one mouse. The other player starts
  the next game.
- **The score** (you, draws, computer) is on the right; the player to move is
  outlined. Each mode keeps its own score; **Reset** clears it.
- **New game**, or a click on a finished board, starts the next game.
- The computer wins when it can, blocks you when it must, and likes the centre
  and corners. A fork beats it.

The game is a card like the notes and terminals: drag it, resize it, let
Arrange place it. It opens by itself the first time the plugin loads. After
that SUPER DESKTOP remembers it: start SUPER DESKTOP again and the game is
there, where you left it, if it was open; closed with ✕, it stays closed.
The small **#** in the top bar opens and closes it. To turn it off
completely, use Settings → Plugins. The game in progress and the score
survive closing the card and restarting SUPER DESKTOP. Colors come from your
Omarchy theme.

## Install

Needs SUPER DESKTOP 1.6.0 or newer.

```sh
super-desktop plugin install https://github.com/gladimdim/super-desktop-tictactoe
super-desktop plugin approve tictactoe
```

Or approve it in Settings → Plugins, where **Ask AI to review** reads it first.

Already installed? `super-desktop plugin update tictactoe`.

## What it does on your PC

- Saves the board, the mode, the score and whether it has shown itself once
  in SUPER DESKTOP's plugin values
  (`~/.local/state/super-desktop/plugins/tictactoe.data.json`).
- Asks SUPER DESKTOP to open or close its own card (`card.open`,
  `card.toggle`). SUPER DESKTOP keeps the card's place and whether it is open
  (`tictactoe.cards.json` next to the values).
- Nothing else: no network, no other files, no programs.

## Change it

It is plain QML: edit a file and SUPER DESKTOP reloads it. `AGENTS.md`
describes how it works for an AI agent; `super-desktop plugin check tictactoe`
and `super-desktop plugin snapshot tictactoe --surface game` check your edits.

## Versions

- **1.1.0**: the game is a card, so SUPER DESKTOP starts with it open or
  closed as you left it. It opens by itself only the first time; # opens and
  closes it.
- **1.0.1**: a closed game stayed closed until # was clicked.
- **1.0.0**: first version.

## License

MIT

one line of what to practise | [README](progress/README.md) | Open it from the link at the bottom of the home page. ## How it works - **Children.** More than one child can play on the same device. A streak of right answers sets off confetti. - **Sound.** Short happy sounds play. Tap the speaker to turn them off. - **Read aloud.** In Plus and Minus, Times and Share, What Time Is It?, Make

# Board Game Builder — simulation engine

A headless game engine, a batch simulator for balance work, and a browser UI
for a loop-board tile game. The UI imports the engine and bots directly and
reimplements no rule.

TypeScript, Node 20+, Vitest, esbuild. No runtime dependencies.

```
engine/     pure engine: types, seeded RNG, board helpers, step / legalActions, describe (readable text), traffic (pass / landing masses)
              engine.ts dispatch + roll / turn flow, effects.ts effect interpreter, attack.ts, loopsShop.ts, endgame.ts,
              shared.ts + sharedBoard.ts the shared-board mode
tiles/      starter tiles, shared-board tiles and landmarks, and die mods as JSON, plus a schema validator
bots/       Random, Greedy, Scorer, Aggressor, Turtle, Expander, Landlord, Builder (weight tables), Lookahead (one-ply EV)
              placement.ts the shared-board, class-aware placement terms
sim/        playGame / replay, batch runner with seat rotation, event-log metrics, CLI, experiments/
web/        browser UI (vanilla TypeScript, esbuild into dist/)
  main.ts       entry: setup screen <-> table screen
  setup.ts      table setup form
  game.ts       wires one game: session, clock, presenter, human controller, table
  loop.ts       async game loop (bot decide / human act -> step -> present)
  human.ts      legal actions -> clickable affordances, resolves with an Action
  presenter.ts  animation queue: plays events beat by beat at the chosen speed
  viewmodel.ts  display model advanced one event at a time
  timing.ts     DURATIONS table, speed scale, pause / step clock
  render/       board (SVG ring), shop, panel (thinking, prompt, log), table, fx
  build.mjs     esbuild bundle + dev server; test/smoke.mjs browser smoke test
tests/      vitest suites, one per build step (web-* cover loop, view model, human)
DECISIONS.md  design decisions, interpretations, and the balance log
```

## Run

```sh
npm install
npm test                 # all suites
npm run typecheck
npm run sim -- batch     # 1000 games, standard lineup, turnCap 15
npm run sim -- batch --games 500 --lineup lookahead,scorer,greedy,turtle --endMode vpRace --endValue 30
npm run sim -- balance   # standard lineup × three end modes + placement value + random floor
npm run sim -- batch --fireOnPass --landBonus 2 --tileEndVp 0.34 --tiles superlinear --endMode vpPool --endValue 60   # experimental variants, off by default
node --import tsx sim/experiments/density.ts   # the variant experiment (about 100 s)
npm run sim -- batch --board shared --lineup random,random,random,random   # shared board mode (see below)
npm run sim -- batch --board shared --sideLength 8 --dice 2d6 --endMode landmarkRace --endValue 3
node --import tsx sim/experiments/shared.ts   # shared board versus loops, ten cells (see sim/experiments/shared-results.md)
node --import tsx sim/experiments/perimeter.ts   # fixed-perimeter shared board and its variant options (sim/experiments/perimeter-results.md)
npm run sim -- batch --board shared --perimeter 24 --catchUp 1 --tollOnPass 0.5 --buyoutPremium 2 --replacementTax 2 --replacementTaxEscalates
npm run sim -- batch --board shared --lineup greedy,scorer,landlord,builder   # the shared-board archetypes
npm run sim -- batch --extended    # loops mode with interaction index and progression (always on in shared mode)
npm run sim -- replay --seed 943   # print one game's event log
npm run sim -- batch --json        # the BatchReport as JSON
npm run dev:web                    # the browser UI on http://localhost:8000 (rebuilds on save)
npm run build:web                  # production bundle into dist/
```

A 1000-game batch of the standard lineup runs in about 2.5 s; `balance` in
about 15 s.

## How it fits together

- **State** is one plain JSON object (`GameState`). `step(state, action)`
  clones, applies, and returns `{ state, events }`. The RNG cursor lives in
  state, so `(seed, actions[])` replays exactly; `sim/runner.ts` has `replay`.
- **Legal acti

tjlytle/techbash-snake.readme:
# battlesnake-platform

A PHP platform for building [Battlesnake](https://play.battlesnake.com/) bots. Bring a strategy class, get a deployable HTTP service.

- **PHP 8.5** with PSR-7/PSR-15 HTTP, PHP-DI 7, EventSauce 3 event sourcing, Doctrine DBAL/ORM/Migrations.
- **SQLite by default** (zero config), **MySQL** optional via a Compose profile.
- **Docker Compose** stack with Caddy + PHP-FPM, plus the official `battlesnake/rules` image for local play.

## Requirements

- Docker + Docker Compose, **or** PHP 8.5 with the `pdo_sqlite`/`pdo_mysql` extensions and Composer.
- `make` (the Makefile wraps the common Compose commands; everything works without it too).

## Quick start

```bash
make build       # build the dev image
make install     # composer install (inside the container)
make migrate     # create the schema in var/snake.db
make up          # start php-fpm + caddy on http://localhost:8088
```

Point the Battlesnake engine (or `make play`) at `http://localhost:8088`. To use a different port: `make up PORT=9099`.

`make help` lists every target.

## Build your snake (3 steps)

### 1. Write

Create a class under `src/Snake/` that implements `BattleSnake\Strategy\Strategy`:

```php
namespace BattleSnake\Snake;

use BattleSnake\Domain\Direction;
use BattleSnake\Domain\GameState;
use BattleSnake\EventSourcing\Game;
use BattleSnake\Strategy\Strategy;

final class MySnake implements Strategy
{
    public function __invoke(Game $game, GameState $state): Direction
    {
        // $state  — the current turn's GameState (board, snakes, you, etc.)
        // $game   — the aggregate; expose history via public read-only props
        return Direction::UP;
    }
}
```

Useful building blocks:

- `src/Domain/` — `Board`, `Battlesnake`, `Coordinate`, `Direction`, `GameState`. Methods like `Board::contains()`, `Board::isThreatenedFor()`, `Battlesnake::couldReach()`, `Coordinate::adjacent()` give you cheap predicates instead of hand-rolled grid math.
- `src/Analyzer/MoveClassifier` — for each direction returns a `Move` flagged `SAFE` / `FOOD` / `END`. `RandomSnake` is the reference consumer.
- `src/Strategy/Aggregate/` — `FirstSafe`, `Majority`, `Scored`, `Conditional`. Composition primitives: each takes `Strategy ...$strategies` and picks one to invoke.
- `src/Strategy/Decorator/` — `Fallback`, `Nudgeable`. Wrap any strategy to add behaviour. `Nudgeable` lets `/manual` override the next move.

### 2. Test

Drop a SnekSpec ASCII board into a PHPUnit test and ask your strategy what it would do:

```
-----
--S--      S = your head, t = your tail
--t--      U/u = opponent, 0 = food, / = hazard
-----
```

See `test/Unit/Domain/BoardTest.php` for the parser pattern. Aggregate-level given/when/then scenarios live in `test/Unit/EventSourcing/GameTest.php` (extend `BattleSnake\Tests\Support\AggregateRootTestCase`).

Run: `make test`.

### 3. Wire

Edit `src/Core/di/snake.php` and point the `Strategy::class` binding at your class:

```php
return [
    Strategy::class => DI\get(MySnake::class),
    MySnake::class  => DI\autowire(),
];
```

Restart (`make restart`) and your snake is live at `/`, `/start`, `/move`, `/end`.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path     | Notes                                                         |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/`      | Battlesnake `info` response.                                  |
| POST   | `/start` | Engine notifies us a game is starting.                        |
| POST   | `/move`  | Engine asks for a move; returns `{"move":"up\|down\|left\|right"}`. |
| POST   | `/end`   | Engine notifies us a game ended; stats row gets written.      |
| POST   | `/manual`| Push a one-shot direction nudge for the next `/move`. Requires the `Nudgeable` decorator (default).|

The OpenAPI spec is checked into `open-api.yaml` and is enforced by the Behat scenario.

## Configuration

| Env var      | Default                                          | No

# TankHit

**Play it:** https://jackgary86-dev.github.io/TankHit/

**Download:** installers for Windows (.exe), macOS (.dmg) and Linux (.AppImage / .deb) are attached to every [GitHub Release](https://github.com/jackgary86-dev/TankHit/releases/latest). The desktop app runs fully offline.

Armor penetration sandbox. Pick a tank, a round and an angle, fire, then watch an X-ray cutaway replay of the penetrator, spall, ballistic-gel crew dummies and ammunition cook-off.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # play at http://localhost:5173
npm test        # simulation unit tests
npm run build   # production build in dist/
npm run desktop # run the Electron desktop app
npm run package # build installers into release/ (current OS)
npm run smoke   # launch the desktop app, run its self-test, exit
```

Releases: push a tag like `v0.2.0` and the `Release installers` workflow builds all three platforms and attaches them to the release. It can also be run from the Actions tab (choose a tag/branch and whether to publish as a draft), and the `CI` workflow can be run manually to produce a Windows installer as a downloadable artifact without cutting a release.

## Modes

- **Sandbox** – free fire, every round unlocked; damage carries over until you hit *Repair vehicle*.
- **Challenges** – eleven puzzles with fixed rounds/range and a shot limit; 1–3 stars by shots used, and stars unlock the later puzzles.
- **Share link** – every shot can be reproduced from its URL (vehicle, round, range, aim, seed, turret yaw).
- **Compare Rounds** – fire up to four rounds at the same point on a fresh tank with the same seed and compare side by side.
- **Duel** – turn-based fight against an AI tank; both sides keep their damage, crew losses matter, the AI aims at your weakest spot.
- **Daily** – one scenario per day for everyone, three attempts, shareable result.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Mouse drag / wheel | Orbit / zoom |
| Click armor | Lock aim point (hover previews LOS and penetration) |
| Space | Fire (or Compare) |
| Esc | Clear aim |
| X | X-ray view (again: back to Painted) |
| C | Cut view: the painted tank sliced open along the shot with solid, layered cross-sections; press again to cut facing the camera |
| Shift+C | Cutaway view: X-ray with the section plane |
| H | Armour map view: plates coloured by thickness |
| K | Kill-map view: knock-out probability across the silhouette (Monte-Carlo, computed in a worker) |
| G | Gunner's sight: real shell drop, time of flight, dispersion; drag to traverse, wheel to zoom |
| Q / E | Traverse the turret |
| V | Auto camera (frames each impact) |
| P / Enter | Play / pause replay |
| A / D | Previous / next shot |
| W / S (+Shift) | Ride the camera along the shot path |
| R | Reset camera |
| M | Mute |

## Vehicles

M4A3 (76) W Sherman, T-34-85, Panther G, Tiger I, IS-3, T-55, M48 Patton, T-72B, M1 Abrams, Leopard 2A4 and Challenger 1 – each is a data file in `src/data/vehicles/` built with the helpers in `src/data/builder.ts`. Add a tank by adding a file and registering it in `src/data/vehicles/index.ts`.

## Simulation

`src/sim/` is pure TypeScript (no three.js) and fully unit-tested:

- **Kinetic** – simplified Lanz–Odermatt (long rods, DU self-sharpening) and de Marre (full-calibre AP/APHE), velocity drop-off, normalization, ricochet and overmatch.
- **Chemical** – HEAT jets (standoff loss, ERA, composite CE multipliers), HESH scabbing, APHE fuze delay bursts, HE blast and thin-plate penetration.
- **Spall** – cones raycast through modules and gel dummies with energy loss per hit.
- **Crew** – zone HP, wound channels, incapacitation and station loss.
- **Cook-off** – ignition rolls, propagation through racks, detonation or blow-out-panel venting; wet stowage quenches most ignitions.
- **Ballistics** – point-mass arc with drag for the gunner's sight; superelevation solved per range.

## Mods

Vehicles and rounds can be added as JSON files without rebuilding: use *Mods* in the top bar

tjlytle/techbash-snake-overnight.readme:
# battlesnake-platform

A PHP platform for building [Battlesnake](https://play.battlesnake.com/) bots. Bring a strategy class, get a deployable HTTP service.

- **PHP 8.5** with PSR-7/PSR-15 HTTP, PHP-DI 7, EventSauce 3 event sourcing, Doctrine DBAL/ORM/Migrations.
- **SQLite by default** (zero config), **MySQL** optional via a Compose profile.
- **Docker Compose** stack with Caddy + PHP-FPM, plus the official `battlesnake/rules` image for local play.

## Requirements

- Docker + Docker Compose, **or** PHP 8.5 with the `pdo_sqlite`/`pdo_mysql` extensions and Composer.
- `make` (the Makefile wraps the common Compose commands; everything works without it too).

## Quick start

```bash
make build       # build the dev image
make install     # composer install (inside the container)
make migrate     # create the schema in var/snake.db
make up          # start php-fpm + caddy on http://localhost:8088
```

Point the Battlesnake engine (or `make play`) at `http://localhost:8088`. To use a different port: `make up PORT=9099`.

`make help` lists every target.

## Build your snake (3 steps)

### 1. Write

Create a class under `src/Snake/` that implements `BattleSnake\Strategy\Strategy`:

```php
namespace BattleSnake\Snake;

use BattleSnake\Domain\Direction;
use BattleSnake\Domain\GameState;
use BattleSnake\EventSourcing\Game;
use BattleSnake\Strategy\Strategy;

final class MySnake implements Strategy
{
    public function __invoke(Game $game, GameState $state): Direction
    {
        // $state  — the current turn's GameState (board, snakes, you, etc.)
        // $game   — the aggregate; expose history via public read-only props
        return Direction::UP;
    }
}
```

Useful building blocks:

- `src/Domain/` — `Board`, `Battlesnake`, `Coordinate`, `Direction`, `GameState`. Methods like `Board::contains()`, `Board::isThreatenedFor()`, `Battlesnake::couldReach()`, `Coordinate::adjacent()` give you cheap predicates instead of hand-rolled grid math.
- `src/Analyzer/MoveClassifier` — for each direction returns a `Move` flagged `SAFE` / `FOOD` / `END`. `RandomSnake` is the reference consumer.
- `src/Strategy/Aggregate/` — `FirstSafe`, `Majority`, `Scored`, `Conditional`. Composition primitives: each takes `Strategy ...$strategies` and picks one to invoke.
- `src/Strategy/Decorator/` — `Fallback`, `Nudgeable`. Wrap any strategy to add behaviour. `Nudgeable` lets `/manual` override the next move.

### 2. Test

Drop a SnekSpec ASCII board into a PHPUnit test and ask your strategy what it would do:

```
-----
--S--      S = your head, t = your tail
--t--      U/u = opponent, 0 = food, / = hazard
-----
```

See `test/Unit/Domain/BoardTest.php` for the parser pattern. Aggregate-level given/when/then scenarios live in `test/Unit/EventSourcing/GameTest.php` (extend `BattleSnake\Tests\Support\AggregateRootTestCase`).

Run: `make test`.

### 3. Wire

Edit `src/Core/di/snake.php` and point the `Strategy::class` binding at your class:

```php
return [
    Strategy::class => DI\get(MySnake::class),
    MySnake::class  => DI\autowire(),
];
```

Restart (`make restart`) and your snake is live at `/`, `/start`, `/move`, `/end`.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path     | Notes                                                         |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/`      | Battlesnake `info` response.                                  |
| POST   | `/start` | Engine notifies us a game is starting.                        |
| POST   | `/move`  | Engine asks for a move; returns `{"move":"up\|down\|left\|right"}`. |
| POST   | `/end`   | Engine notifies us a game ended; stats row gets written.      |
| POST   | `/manual`| Push a one-shot direction nudge for the next `/move`. Requires the `Nudgeable` decorator (default).|

The OpenAPI spec is checked into `open-api.yaml` and is enforced by the Behat scenario.

## Configuration

| Env var      | Default                                          | No

lucassingh/bizit-games.readme:
# Bizit Game Center

PWA de la expo de **Bizit Global**: tres juegos con **BGen** (la mascota de BGenAI) que captan leads para el CRM Odoo.
Funciona en TV (45–55") y tablets, con Wi-Fi malo o sin conexión.

> Contexto, guiones y decisiones: `../docs/` (empezar por `docs/CLAUDE.md`). Arquitectura: `../docs/10-arquitectura-app.md`.

## Arrancar

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # por defecto ODOO_MODE=mock (no envía nada)
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:3000
```

| Script | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Desarrollo (el service worker no se registra en dev) |
| `npm run build && npm start` | Producción local (con service worker → probar offline) |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint (config de Next 16) |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript sin emitir |
| `npm test` | Vitest: puntaje, fases, armado del lead de Odoo |

## Desplegar en Vercel

1. Importar el repo en Vercel (framework: Next.js, sin cambios).
2. Cargar las variables de `.env.example` (Settings → Environment Variables). Para enviar leads reales: `ODOO_MODE=jsonrpc` (o `json2` en Odoo 19+), `ODOO_URL`, `ODOO_DB`, `ODOO_LOGIN`, `ODOO_API_KEY`.
3. Probar `GET /api/health`.

## En la expo (checklist)

1. Con Wi-Fi, abrir la app en cada dispositivo y dejarla 15 s en la pantalla de inicio: precarga los 3 juegos para usarlos sin red.
2. Instalarla como app (Chrome → "Instalar app" / "Agregar a pantalla de inicio") y abrirla en pantalla completa.
3. Mantener apretado el logo de Bizit 3 s → **/config**: nombre del dispositivo, stand, vista (TV/tablet), juegos habilitados, duración. Ahí también se ven los leads del dispositivo y se fuerza el envío.
4. Los leads se guardan en el dispositivo (IndexedDB) y se envían solos al volver la conexión. No borrar los datos del navegador antes de ver "0 pendientes" en /config.

## Estructura

```
src/
  app/                 page (una sola página, máquina de estados), /config, /api/leads, /api/health, manifest
  components/          Experience (flujo), screens/ (attract, registro, selector, briefing, juego, resultado), hud/, BGen
  games/
    compania/          Juego 1 · runner 3D (Three.js)
    deploy/            Juego 2 · física (Matter.js + Canvas 2D)
    central/           Juego 3 · ruteo de tareas (Canvas 2D)
    shared/            reloj de fases, puntaje con combos, gestos, cara LED de BGen
  lib/                 marca, catálogo de juegos, puntaje, cola de leads offline, Odoo, ranking
public/sw.js           service worker offline-first
```

Depuración: `/?debug` expone el estado de la física de Deploy en `window.__deploy`.

jayancey/Morrowind-ScavengerScramble.desc: Scavenger Scramble: a round-based scavenger-hunt game mode for TES3MP (Morrowind multiplayer)
jayancey/Morrowind-ScavengerScramble.readme:
# Scavenger Scramble

A scavenger-hunt game mode for [TES3MP](https://github.com/TES3MP/TES3MP) (Morrowind multiplayer), built for the 0.8.1 CoreScripts API and dfashbaugh's OpenMW 0.51 port. Tamriel Rebuilt cities are supported out of the box because every location and item pool is generated from the server's real load order.

## How a round works

1. A staff member runs `/scramble start` (optionally with a length in minutes). Everyone online is teleported to the chosen city, its cells are reset to pristine, and three objectives are announced: by default one exact item that is known to exist in that city plus two categories such as "any dagger" or "any item worth 500+ gold".
2. Players scramble. Buying, stealing, pickpocketing, looting corpses and robbing each other are all fair. Leaving the city gives a warning and a short grace period, then a teleport back.
3. When the real-time timer ends, inventories are checked. Only items gained during the round count.
4. The showcase cell (Nerano Manor by default) is reset to pristine, which clears earlier displays and anything that was spawned or killed there, and everyone is moved into it. Players drop their finds to display them, then type `/scramble done`.
5. Scoring: 1 point per objective satisfied, plus 1 bonus point for the most valuable item in each category. Ties break on total value, then on who finished displaying first. Results are announced in chat and a scoreboard, and wins are tracked across rounds.

## Commands

| Command | Who | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/scramble start [minutes]` | staff | Start a round at the next location |
| `/scramble stop` | staff | Abort the round |
| `/scramble location [name, number, random, list]` | staff | Pick the next location (no argument opens a list box) |
| `/scramble minutes <n>` | staff | Default round length |
| `/scramble score` | staff | End the showcase early and score |
| `/scramble reset` | staff | Clear a stuck round without scoring |
| `/scramble here` | staff | Print your position as a spawn override line |
| `/scramble showcase` | staff | Make where you stand the showcase spot (persists across restarts) |
| `/scramble objectives` | all | Show the objectives again |
| `/scramble status` | all | Phase, time left, participants |
| `/scramble done` / `pass` | all | Finish your showcase display |
| `/scramble results` / `leaderboard` | all | Last results and all-time wins |

`/ss` is an alias for `/scramble`. Staff means CoreScripts staff rank 1 or higher (see `config.controlRank`).

## Setup

1. Generate the data from your game's load order (needs Python 3.10+, no extra packages):

   ```
   python tools\gen_data.py --cfg "C:\Users\<you>\Documents\My Games\OpenMW\openmw.cfg" --out scavenger-scramble\data
   ```

   See `scavenger-scramble/data/README.md` for options such as skipping plugins.

2. Deploy into the server (backs up any older copy, mirrors the folder, adds the require line to `customScripts.lua`):

   ```
   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\deploy.ps1 -ServerRoot "F:\tes3mp.Win64.release.0.8.1"
   ```

3. Restart `tes3mp-server.exe`. The server log prints `[Scramble] Scavenger Scramble ready`.

4. Tune `scavenger-scramble/config.lua`: round length, objective mix, showcase cell and position, bounds padding, grace time. Hand-picked spawn points go in `data/spawn_overrides.lua` (use `/scramble here` in game to get the line).

## Tests

```
python -m pip install lupa
python tests\run_tests.py          # LuaJIT 2.1, the same Lua the server embeds
python tests\run_tests.py --lua51  # plain Lua 5.1
```

The tests run the real modules against a stubbed TES3MP API with fixture data in `tests/fixtures`.

## Layout

```
scavenger-scramble/   the mod (deployed to server/scripts/custom/scavenger-scramble)
  main.lua            entry point, event hooks
  config.lua          tunables
  round.lua           start, timer, showcase hand-off, results
  objectives.lua      rolling and matching
  scoring.lua         c

SteffanPoulsen/hark.desc: Listen fast, export clean. A local audio asset browser for sound design: games, film, apps, theatre, podcasts.
SteffanPoulsen/hark.readme: **Listen fast, export clean.** A local audio asset browser for anyone who works from a library of sounds: game audio, film and video post, apps, theatre, podcasts, sample packs. ![hark auditioning a sword take, one hit selected with fades, the export card set to the sfx preset](docs/screenshots/hero.png) hark sits between your sound libraries and the project they feed. Point it at the folders the libraries live in, arrow through them at keyboard speed, star and tag what works, select the part you want on the waveform, and export it through a preset into the project's audio folder with a consistent name, format and loudness. Every exported file carries where it came from and how it was made, embedded in the file itself, so months later `hark-cli inspect` still knows. Linux (Wayland) first, Windows and macOS from the same code. No accounts, no subscriptions, no cloud. Free software under the GPL. ## Why Auditioning a big library in a DAW means importing first, and in a file manager means waiting for a player to open; neither remembers what you liked. Exporting by hand gives a different level and format every time, and leaves a file in the project with no link back to the pack it came from. hark does the whole loop in one window, at the speed of the arrow keys, and writes the link into the file. ## Features - **Instant audition.** Arrowing through the list plays each file as it lands: one always-open audio stream, pre-decoded neighbours, cached waveform peaks. Hour-long recordings stream from disk and start as fast as a one-shot. - **Library, not import.** Folders stay where they are and are never modified. A folder lists everything under it, each file with its subfolder, duration, channels, rate, bit depth, codec and loudness; search covers everything, and a filter narrows by favorites, tags, type and channels. - **Favorites and tags** from the keyboard. Tags are yours to define, with a colour each. Marks key on the file's content, so a renamed or moved file keeps them. - **Projects.** A `.hark` file beside the game, the edit or the show holds its library folders, its output folder and its own favorites. Switch between projects from the top bar. - **Waveform selection with fades.** Drag a region or trim it to the sound, step through the takes a recording holds with Left and Right, set fade in and out, zoom, loop, seek by clicking, and scale the level with the fader beside the waveform. - **Preset-driven export.** WAV or FLAC, bit depth with dither, resampling, mono downmix, peak or EBU R128 loudness normalisation under a true-peak ceiling, and a file name template. Override any of it for one export. - **An origin inside every export.** A `hark` RIFF chunk and a BWF `bext` description in WAV, an APPLICATION block and a Vorbis comment in FLAC: source path and hash, pack, selection, fades, preset and measured gain. `hark-cli reexport` runs that recipe again with changes. - **A CLI for all of it.** `hark-cli` exposes the same core with `--json` on every command, so a script or an agent can search, mark, analyse and export without a window. ![The presets page of the settings window](docs/screenshots/presets.png) ## Install Downloads for Linux and Windows are on the [Releases](../../releases) page. To build from source: ``` cargo build --release ``` Binaries land in `target/release/hark` (the window) and `target/release/hark-cli`. `packaging/install.sh` installs the desktop entry and the icon for the current user, so launchers and the compositor show hark by its app id; from a release archive it also puts the binaries in `~/.local/bin`. Rust stable; on Linux the PipeWire headers (`pipewire` package) are needed for the native backend, with ALSA as the fallback. Windows builds with the MSVC or GNU toolchain and uses WASAPI. ## Use Start `hark`, add a library folder with the button under the tree, pick a folder, and arrow through the files. `hark --open ` st

TwentyOOO/emirati-arabizi-translator.readme:
# Emirati Arabizi Translator

Type English, get Emirati Arabic written in Arabizi (Arabic in Latin letters and numbers).
It runs completely offline in your browser: no AI, no server, no account.

**Use it online:** https://twentyooo.github.io/emirati-arabizi-translator/

Or download `index.html`, open it, and type.

| English | Emirati Arabizi |
| --- | --- |
| and then learned a lot more when creating lebot | wba3dain t3allamt wayed akthar lamma kint asawi lebot. |
| i got the item i wanted | 7a99alt il-item illi kint abeeh. |
| does anyone know how to get the void highlord class? | a7ad yadri shlon a7a99il void highlord class? |
| what server are you on? | 3ala ay server inta? |
| hey bro how r u i need help with the bot it keeps crashing | hala 5ooy, shlonak, a7taaj musaa3ada fil-bot, ya6'all y6ee7. |
| cant, gotta study for my exam tmrw smh | ma agdar, laazim adris 7ag imti7aani bacher, uffff. |

## How it works

`src/en2ae.js` is a word list plus Emirati grammar rules: verb tenses and persons, gender and plural,
possession (`il-bot maali`), relative clauses (`illi`), questions, negation and common phrases.
The output is lower case, `and` is joined to the next word (`wba3dain`), and commas and full stops are added.
Chat spelling is understood too: `u`, `ur`, `im`, `ill`, `cant`, `gtg`, `smh`, `ngl`, stretched words like `soooo`, and `cause` for `because`.

- AdventureQuest Worlds item, map and monster names are never translated (`src/aqw_names.json`).
- Put any word in square brackets to keep it as it is: `my [LeBot] is fast` → `LeBot maali saree3.`

## Letters

| Arabic | Arabizi | Arabic | Arabizi |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ء ؤ ئ | 2 | خ | 5 |
| ع | 3 | غ | 3' |
| ط | 6 | ظ | 6' |
| ح | 7 | ص | 9 |
| ض | 9' | ث | th |
| ذ | dh | ش | sh |
| چ | ch | ق | g |

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | The translator, ready to open (everything is inside it). |
| `src/en2ae.js` | The translation engine. |
| `src/aqw_names.json` | Names that are never translated. |
| `assets/` | Interface art (not MIT, see `NOTICE.md`). |
| `build.py` | Rebuilds `index.html` from `src/` and `assets/`. |
| `tests/` | Reviewed translations; `node tests/test.js` checks them. |
| `tools/` | Spelling checks for the word list. |

## Build and test

```
python3 build.py        # writes index.html
node tests/test.js      # 1178 reviewed sentences
```

## License

The code is MIT (see `LICENSE`). The interface art belongs to Artix Entertainment and is not part of
that license, see `NOTICE.md`. This is a fan project and is not affiliated with Artix Entertainment.

BRANDAY/AcousticsLab.readme:
# AcousticsLab

**A test bench in Unreal Engine 5 for the geometric-acoustics methods of Marjan Sikora (FESB, Split)** — stochastic ray tracing, image sources, triangular beam tracing with beam division, beam tracing with refraction, thread-level parallelization and hybrid beam/ray tracing — implemented in C++, drawn in the 3D scene, and made audible by convolution; later to be compared on the same geometry with two production tools, Steam Audio (Valve) and Audio Tracing (Pinpoint).

The aim is to understand the methods by building them and to be able to show them: every method is a mode of the application where you see the rays or beams, the impulse response and the room-acoustic metrics, and hear the result. It is a learning and demonstration project, not a scientific result.

![Beams containing the receiver, beam tracer in the shoebox](docs/guide/img/M5_beams_receiver_crop.png)

*Beam tracer in the 10 × 7 × 3 m validation room: the beams of orders 2–3 that contain receiver R1 (orange, red), the simulation panel, and the impulse response with the discrete early arrivals.*

**→ Reviewer's guide: [docs/guide](docs/guide/README.md) · 10-minute tour: [docs/guide/walkthrough.md](docs/guide/walkthrough.md)**

moonloch/dcc-core-lib.desc: Pure-function TypeScript library for Dungeon Crawl Classics RPG game logic
moonloch/dcc-core-lib.readme:
# @moonloch/dcc-core-lib

[![CI](https://github.com/moonloch/dcc-core-lib/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/moonloch/dcc-core-lib/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Game logic for the Dungeon Crawl Classics (DCC) RPG as a TypeScript library: dice chain, checks and saves, combat, spellcasting, character creation and advancement. It is built from pure functions with no platform dependencies, so it runs in Node.js, browsers, FoundryVTT, or anywhere else JavaScript does.

> **This repository contains no DCC RPG book text.** There is no rules prose, table text, spell description or flavor text from any Goodman Games publication anywhere in the code, tests or docs. Official tables and results are referred to by name only, and test fixtures use placeholder or altered values.

The library is **logic only**. It ships no official rulebook data either: class progressions, spell results, crit and fumble tables and the like are registered at runtime by the app that uses the library, from a data source built from the app's own licensed copy. [docs/DATA.md](docs/DATA.md) explains how.

The main consumer is the [DCC system for FoundryVTT](https://github.com/foundryvtt-dcc/dcc), which vendors this library's build. Game-logic fixes for that system belong here, with a regression test; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Status

- **Stage:** pre-1.0 and actively maintained. Minor versions can change the API; breaking changes are called out in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).
- **In production:** the DCC system for FoundryVTT runs its rolls, checks, saves, combat and spellcasting through this library.
- **Rules accuracy:** behavior is checked against the rules as written and covered by unit tests, and every bug fix lands with a regression test. Known gaps are tracked as [open issues](https://github.com/moonloch/dcc-core-lib/issues).
- **Releases:** listed on the [releases page](https://github.com/moonloch/dcc-core-lib/releases) and published to GitHub Packages.
- **Variants:** a `SystemConfig` type for DCC variants such as MCC and XCrawl exists, with the DCC config shipped as `DCC_SYSTEM`, but no function takes it yet. See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#system-variants-mcc-xcrawl-etc).

## Installation

The package is **not** on the public npm registry, and the unscoped name `dcc-core-lib` is not this package. There are three ways to consume it:

### 1. Vendored by the DCC FoundryVTT system (primary consumer)

FoundryVTT has no bundler, so the [DCC system](https://github.com/foundryvtt-dcc/dcc) commits this library's built `dist/` into `module/vendor/dcc-core-lib/` and imports it directly. The system repo's `scripts/sync-core-lib.mjs` builds a local checkout of this repo and copies `dist/` across (writing `VERSION.json` with the source commit). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#how-a-fix-reaches-the-dcc-system).

### 2. GitHub Packages

Each GitHub release publishes `@moonloch/dcc-core-lib` to GitHub Packages. GitHub Packages' npm registry requires authentication even for public packages, so you need a personal access token (classic) with the `read:packages` scope.

```ini
# .npmrc (project or ~/.npmrc) — do not commit the token
@moonloch:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN}
```

```bash
pnpm add @moonloch/dcc-core-lib
# or
npm install @moonloch/dcc-core-lib
```

### 3. From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/moonloch/dcc-core-lib.git
cd dcc-core-lib
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build   # emits dist/
```

## Quick start

```typescript
import {
  evaluateRoll,
  bumpDie,
  getAbilityModifier,
  createZeroLevelCharacter,
  DEFAULT_CHARACTER_CREATION_DATA,
  defaultRandomSource,
  rollAbilityCheck,
  rollSavingThrow,
} from '@moonloch/dcc-core-lib';

// Dice and the dice chain
evaluateRoll('1d20+3', { mode: 'evaluate' }).total; // e.g. 17
bumpDie('1d20', 1);    // '1d24'
bumpDie('1d20', -2);   // '1d14'
getAbilityModifier(16); // 2

// A random 0-

parkerfellows/quidditch.desc: Single-file browser Quidditch game with peer-to-peer online play
parkerfellows/quidditch.readme:
# Quidditch

A single-file arcade Quidditch match for the browser. No build step, no dependencies: open `quidditch.html` and play.

## Play

- Pick your house, your opponent and a difficulty, then click **Mount Your Broom**.
- You fly your house's lead Chaser. Score with the Quaffle (10 points), dodge Bludgers, and catch the Snitch (150 points, ends the match) before the AI Seekers do.

### Controls

| Action | Input |
| --- | --- |
| Fly | Move the mouse (or WASD / arrow keys) |
| Boost | Hold Shift or Space |
| Shoot | Left click. Point at a hoop to pick it, or auto-aim at the open one |
| Pass | Right click or Q |
| Steal | Ram the Quaffle carrier at speed |
| Pause / Mute | P / M |

## Online two-player

Peer-to-peer over WebRTC, no server required.

1. The host picks the houses and clicks **Host a match**, then sends the generated code to a friend.
2. The friend clicks **Join a match**, pastes the code, clicks **Generate reply**, and sends the reply code back.
3. The host pastes the reply and clicks **Connect**. The match starts on both screens.

The host runs the match and streams state to the guest. Some strict corporate or mobile networks block direct peer connections; a TURN relay would be needed for those.

suhdonghwi/invariant-frog.desc: A puzzle game about loop invariants, checked by Z3
suhdonghwi/invariant-frog.readme:
# Invariant Frog

An interactive, visual website that teaches programmers what loop invariants are — by drawing an area that frogs can never hop out of.

- Each tile on an endless white plane is one program state; a **frog** hops once per loop iteration.
- You write a formula for an **area** (the loop invariant); tiles inside it rise as slabs.
- **Check** tests three rules — Initialization, Maintenance, Termination — and, when one fails, shows a see-through **ghost frog** that breaks your area.
- Inputs that never change (like `n`, or an array `A`) become **planes**, one per value, picked in the inputs card under the code.
- Read-only arrays: `A[k]`, and `forall` / `exists` over a range of cells, with Z3 proving the quantified rules.
- In English and Korean (한국어), switched on the home screen.

Docs:

- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) — what the game teaches, the rules of its world, and the tutorial's vocabulary
- [docs/experience.md](docs/experience.md) — how the interface should look, move and respond
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — how the code is organised, and the rules that keep it working

## Running

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

The solver (Z3 compiled to WebAssembly) needs a cross-origin isolated page, so the dev and preview servers send
`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. Any production host must send
the same headers. `pnpm install` copies Z3's browser build into `public/z3/`.

## Scripts

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pnpm dev` | Dev server |
| `pnpm test` | Unit tests (parser, types, integer semantics, box search) |
| `pnpm validate` | Proves every level's solutions with Z3, checks every pitfall fails the intended rule, checks real frogs terminate, and checks no hint gives a solution away |
| `pnpm build` | Typecheck + production build |

chvolk/PortalShifter.desc: Car-combat racing with portals: Destruction Derby meets Splitgate, built in Unity
chvolk/PortalShifter.readme:
# PortalShift

Car combat racing with portals: Wreckfest-style wrecking, Destruction Derby modes, Splitgate-style portals you shoot onto walls
to take shortcuts in a race or get the drop on someone in the arena. Unity 6000.2.12f1, URP, Netcode for GameObjects (LAN),
Input System (Xbox controller first).

Modes: **3-Lap Race** (respawns), **Deathrace** (no respawns, last driver rolling wins) on *Canyon Run*;
**Battle** (last car standing) in *The Pit*. Solo vs AI, or host/join over LAN with AI filling the grid.

## Build

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\build.ps1 -Setup     # first time (layers, player settings, TMP)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\build.ps1            # regenerate assets/scenes + build dist\PortalShift
```

Everything in `Assets/PortalShift/Generated` and `Assets/PortalShift/Scenes` is produced by the editor scripts in
`Assets/PortalShift/Editor` (menu *PortalShift* inside Unity does the same). Textures come from `tools/fetch-textures.py`
(Poly Haven, CC0). Third-party models and recordings live in `assets/` with their licences:

```
blender.exe -b --python tools/blender-import-cars.py  -- unity\PortalShift\Assets\PortalShift\Models\Cars    # CC-BY cars -> FBX + textures + manifest
blender.exe -b --python tools/blender-import-props.py -- unity\PortalShift\Assets\PortalShift\Models\Props   # Poly Haven props, decimated
blender.exe -b --python tools/blender-audio.py        -- <out>   # engine/tyre/impact loops, copy to Assets\PortalShift\Resources\Audio
```

Attributions required by the CC-BY assets are on the in-game Credits screen; the full lists are
`assets/models/LICENSES.md` and `assets/audio/LICENSES.md`.

## Test

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\autotest.ps1 -Mode race -Bots 7 -Duration 120
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\autotest.ps1 -Mode battle -Lan
```

Runs the build unattended (AI drives the local car), prints `[AT]` stats, drops screenshots in `dist\autotest\<stamp>\shots`.
`-Extra @('-debugcol','-drifttest','-portaltest')` adds collision logging, a scripted handbrake/corner test and a portal
aim/drive-through test.

## Cloning

Two large download-only folders are not in git: the Poly Haven texture sets (`tools/fetch-textures.py` restores them,
the tracked `.meta` files keep the asset GUIDs stable) and the raw third-party model downloads under `assets/models/`
(every source URL is in `assets/models/LICENSES.md`; the processed FBX files the game uses are tracked). `tools/unity.ps1`
finds the editor through Unity Hub's default install folder, or set `UNITY_EDITOR` to the path of `Unity.exe`.

## Portal rules

Every concrete boundary slab takes a portal. In a race the two portals of a pair may be at most 200 m apart measured
along the lap (not as the crow flies); placing one further away closes its partner. The reticle turns red to warn.

## Controls (Xbox)

RT gas, LT brake/reverse, LS steer, A nitro, B handbrake, RB machine gun, LB rocket, X slam (melee lunge),
Y drop mine/oil, D-pad left/right switch mine/oil, D-pad up blue portal, D-pad down orange portal, RS aim camera,
RS click look back, LS click reset car, Start pause, Back scoreboard.
Keyboard: WASD, Shift, Space, LMB/RMB, F, E, Q, 1/2, mouse aim, C, R, Esc, Tab.

NoobyGains/brawllive.desc: In-game online matchmaking for Project+ (Brawl) on the official Dolphin netplay build
NoobyGains/brawllive.readme:
🥊 BrawlLive

Press a button on your pad. Get a match. Play.
Online matchmaking for Project+ that lives inside the game window, on the official netplay build.

--- ## 🎯 Why Project+ is where competitive Brawl lives, and getting a game still means posting host codes in Discord and waiting. Slippi showed what happens when matchmaking moves into the game itself: a community forms around the queue. BrawlLive brings that loop to P+ without waiting for rollback netcode and without breaking compatibility with anyone on the stock build. ## 🎮 What the player does | Step | What happens | |---|---| | 1️⃣ **Install once** | Run the installer. It swaps one file, `Dolphin.exe`, inside your existing P+ 3.2 folder and keeps the original as a backup. No account, no sign-up. | | 2️⃣ **Launch P+ as usual** | A small BrawlLive overlay appears in the game window. | | 3️⃣ **Hold L + R + Start** | The menu opens: Casual or Ranked, Singles or Doubles. Pick with the D-pad, confirm with A. | | 4️⃣ **Keep playing while you wait** | CPU matches, training, whatever. The overlay shows the search. | | 5️⃣ **Match found** | Opponent and ping on screen, a short countdown, then Dolphin restarts straight into the netplay session with the buffer already set. | | 6️⃣ **After the game** | Rematch or requeue from the same overlay. | > 🧩 **Stock-compatible.** BrawlLive players can still join ordinary P+ 3.2 lobbies by code. The patched build changes nothing in the emulation core, and CI enforces that. ## 🏗️ How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph PC["🎮 Player's PC"] D["BrawlLive Dolphin.exe
P+ 3.2 fork, frontend-only patch"] O["🖼️ In-game overlay
pad combos"] A["📡 Agent
HTTPS long-poll"] D --- O D --- A end S["🧠 Matchmaking service
Node.js · PostgreSQL"] T["🔀 Traversal server
Dolphin's own, self-hosted"] W["🌐 Website
leaderboards · profiles · download"] A <-- "commands / events" --> S D <-- "Dolphin NetPlay over UDP" --> T S --- W ``` - **Agent in Dolphin.** A headless client long-polls the service for `host`, `join` and `start` commands and reports `hosting`, `player_joined`, `game_started`, `game_ended`. - **Overlay.** Drawn with the same ImGui layer Dolphin uses for netplay chat, driven by the emulated pad state so GameCube adapters work with zero setup. - **Service.** Queues, pairing by region, ping band and rating, a match state machine with a timeout and recovery for every stage. - **Identity.** Zero-signup device identity. Discord linking comes later and may be required for ranked. ## 🗺️ Roadmap | # | Sub-project | Status | |---|---|---| | 1 | 🔧 **Dolphin build**: agent, overlay, combos, installer, stub server, CI | 🟡 planned, [14 tasks ready](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-brawllive-dolphin-build.md) | | 2 | 🧠 **Matchmaking service core**: casual singles, pairing, host-code relay, traversal server | ⚪ next | | 3 | 🌐 **Website**: download, guide, status, leaderboards | ⚪ | | 4 | 🏆 **Ranked**: ratings, result claims and disputes, then in-emulator result capture | ⚪ | | 5 | 👥 **Doubles**: four-player sessions, team queue | ⚪ | | 6 | 🚀 **Operations and launch**: E

# Last Cans

A single-player post-apocalyptic extraction game for iPhone Safari. Go topside,
scavenge pre-collapse hard seltzer cans, and get back to the lift before the
storm rolls in. Same zone for everyone each day, one official run, share your haul.

Debug: `?zone=N` plays any zone without saving results (phase 3+).

Phase 5: storm visuals, lighting, weather audio, title fly-over

The storm now rolls in: cloud shadows drift over the ground and speed
up, wind-blown debris streaks across the screen, a dark red front
creeps down from the top, lightning flashes with thunder trailing it,
and rain falls in the last twenty seconds. A half-resolution lighting
pass darkens the world as the storm nears and cuts holes for the

Wordle-style text and uses navigato

from the spawn. validateZone checks r

Skitters sit idle and rush toward noise (footsteps, rummaging, thrown
cans, lift calls) and chase on sight. Spotter drones fly patrol loops
sweeping a raycast scan beam; being lit fills the alert meter, and a
full meter makes the drone screech, dive, and call nearby machines.
One strider patrols the north with a long floodlight cone, locks on,
charges, and calls everything. Any machine contact downs the player.

guelowrd/pub.readme:
# Pick Up Boomers

Three-minute arcade drive: pick up boomers, deliver them to where they spend, most points wins.
High scores go onchain with GeoQuizz's record/shot notes on Miden.

Plan and decisions: `tasks/todo.md`. Art briefs: `docs/designer-brief.md`, `docs/designer-brief-next.md`.

```
cd web && yarn && yarn dev                      # http://localhost:5173
cd web && yarn test                             # 67 tests: sim, rules, chain packing, note flows, boards, the hashes
cargo test -p integration --test pub_test       # the MASM replay against rules/vectors.json (4 tests, ~1 min)
cargo run --bin build_scripts                   # assembles the two note scripts into web/public/scripts/
```

Keys: arrows or WASD drive, p pauses, m mutes. In the head unit: 1-6 pick a mode, arrows move or tune, Enter selects,
Esc goes back, AUTO is the action on the lower display.

Onchain: a run can be posted as a record (a Gamecoin prize on it); rivals pay a Gamecoin for a shot at its course and
song and must beat the score; the chain replays the decision log (`masm/games/pub_score.masm`). Bread signs; without it,
`?local=1` and `?local=2` run two test wallets inside the app (fee-funded from the testnet faucet, Gamecoins from the
WALLET mode). Note tag 0x50420001, scripts in `web/public/scripts/`.

Deploy: Vercel, root directory `web` (`web/vercel.json` sets the cross-origin isolation headers the Miden client needs).

# TLG — The LAN Game: **Kerker**

Asymmetrisches Browser-Spiel für die LAN: **einer baut den Kerker, die anderen
holen das Artefakt — dann wird getauscht.** 2 bis 16 Spieler, Matches von 8 bis
20 Minuten, nur ein Browser am PC. Nutzerverwaltung kommt komplett von
[Craftworks](https://github.com/Phat-shot/craftworks); TLG hat keine eigene
Datenbank.

## Spielprinzip

- **Helden** (Top-Down, WASD + Maus) starten am Eingang, müssen das **Artefakt**
  am entferntesten Punkt holen und zum **Ausgang** tragen — der liegt bewusst
  nahe am Eingang: rein, holen, denselben Weg zurück. Der Träger ist langsamer.
  Das Team sieht nur, was ein lebender Held sieht (Sichtradius + Sichtlinie),
  und hat einen gemeinsamen Lebensvorrat (2 pro Held); danach ist ein Tod endgültig.
- **Der Kerker** sieht alles und setzt in Echtzeit Karten gegen **Mana**
  (regeneriert, +25 pro Kill): Stachelfalle und Fallgrube (für Helden
  unsichtbar, bis sie auslösen oder ein Schurke sie aufdeckt), Mauer (60 HP,
  darf den Kerker **nie versiegeln** — der Server prüft Eingang→Ausgang,
  Eingang→Artefakt und jeden Helden→Ausgang), Krabbler, Brecher, Nebel
  (Sicht auf 2,5 Kacheln). Nichts darf näher als 4 Kacheln (Monster: 6) an einem
  lebenden Helden gesetzt werden.
- **Klassen**: Krieger (Schildstoß: Dash + Rammstoß, haut Mauern weg),
  Schütze (Salve), Heiler (Heilkreis), Schurke (Spürsinn: deckt Fallen auf,
  3 s unsichtbar).
- **Sieg**: Helden, wenn das Artefakt den Ausgang erreicht. Kerker, wenn die
  Zeit abläuft oder alle Helden ohne Leben tot sind.
- **Serie mit festen Teams**: Der Host legt die Spieler pro Team fest (2er-Teams
  ab 4 Spielern, 3er ab 6 usw. — es müssen immer mindestens 2 Teams entstehen;
  7 Spieler bei 2er-Teams ergeben 3, 2, 2). Teams werden automatisch verteilt,
  der Host kann verschieben oder neu mischen. **Runden = Teams**: jedes Team ist
  genau einmal Kerker, die übrigen Teams fliehen gemeinsam, pro Runde eine neue
  Karte. 6 Spieler in 2er-Teams heißt 3 Runden, je 2 Kerkermeister gegen 4 Helden.
- **Punkte**: Kerker-Sieg 3 fürs Kerker-Team. Helden-Sieg 2 für jedes Heldenteam,
  +1 fürs Team des Artefakt-Trägers. Nach der letzten Runde steht das Siegerteam.
  Verlässt ein ganzes Team die Serie, entfällt seine Kerker-Runde.

Alle Zahlen stehen in `packages/shared/src/constants.js`.

## Architektur

```
packages/shared/   Konstanten, Kartengenerator (Seed-deterministisch), BFS/A*, Sichtlinie — Server UND Client
server/            Express + Socket.io, ein Worker-Thread pro Match (server/src/match/worker.js)
  src/match/engine.js   reine Engine: step(), placeCard(), snapshotFor() — ohne Timer, ohne Sockets
  src/lobby.js          Lobbys im Speicher, Teams, Serie (Runden, Punkte)
  src/auth.js           Craftworks-Anbindung (Token-Prüfung + Auth-Proxy)
client/            Vite + TypeScript, Canvas-Renderer, kein Framework
```

**Server ist autoritativ**, Clients zeigen nur an. `snapshotFor()` ist die
einzige Stelle, die Zustand herausgibt, und filtert pro Rolle: Helden bekommen
nie versteckte Fallen, nie Monster außer Sicht, nie Kerker-Mana, nie
Platzierungs-Ereignisse. Pro Tick (20 Hz) werden genau zwei Snapshots
gerechnet — Helden-Teamsicht und Kerker-Sicht.

### Craftworks-Anbindung (keine Änderung an Craftworks nötig)

- Der Browser spricht nur mit TLG. `/api/auth/*` (login, guest, refresh,
  logout, config, register, magic-link) wird 1:1 an `CRAFTWORKS_URL` weitergereicht —
  deshalb braucht Craftworks keine CORS-Freigabe für TLG.
- Ein Access-Token gilt, wenn Craftworks' `GET /api/users/me` ihn annimmt
  (60 s gecacht). Beim Socket-Handshake genauso. Kein geteiltes JWT-Secret.
- Gast-Login (Craftworks `/api/auth/guest`) ist der Normalweg auf der LAN; dafür
  muss in Craftworks `guest_login_enabled` an sein.

## Starten

```bash
npm ci
npm test                     # Shared + Engine + Lobby + Auth + End-to-End über echte Sockets
npm run build                # Client nach client/dist
CRAFTWORKS_URL=https://dev.srz.one npm start

NotRithik/edge-city-game-jam-promptcraft.readme:
# PromptCraft

A Minecraft-like voxel sandbox in a single HTML page, where an AI (Google **Gemini 4 Argon** by default, or Claude) builds structures and invents new blocks, creatures, items and world rules while you play. AI agents (like **Ada**, the architect) live in the world and build on their own.

```
promptcraft/
  server.js          tiny Node server: serves the game, calls the AI, enforces password + $ budget
  prompt.md          the AI's manual (system prompt) for the action language; edit it to teach the AI new tricks
  public/index.html  the whole game: voxel engine, creatures, action-language VM, UI (Three.js from CDN)
  data/usage.json    running $ spend (delete it to reset the budget counter)
```

## Run it

```bash
cd promptcraft
npm install
cp .env.example .env    # then set GEMINI_API_KEY and GAME_PASSWORD (budget defaults to $100)
npm start               # http://localhost:8787
```

**Live:** play at **https://edge-city-mc-univ.vercel.app**.
- **Frontend:** `public/index.html` on Vercel, project `edge-city-mc-univ`. Redeploy with `vercel deploy public --prod --yes --project edge-city-mc-univ`.
- **Backend:** the API only, running as the `edge-city-mc-univ` Docker container on the AWS VM (18.207.103.187). The VM's Caddy serves it at `https://edge-city-mc-univ.18-207-103-187.nip.io` and forwards to `127.0.0.1:18787`. Redeploy with `./deploy.sh` after changing `server.js`, `prompt.md` or `.env`. The spend counter lives on the VM in `~/edge-city-mc-univ/data/usage.json`.
- **Local:** when opened from localhost, the page calls its own server (`npm start`). Anywhere else, it calls the AWS backend (`API_BASE` in `index.html`).

To share a local copy instead, run `npm run tunnel` in a second terminal. It starts a Cloudflare quick tunnel and prints a `https://*.trycloudflare.com` URL.

- **Password:** players type `GAME_PASSWORD` in the menu (Esc) to unlock the AI. Without it the game still works, but nothing is sent to the model. If you don't set one, the server makes one up and prints it at startup. 10 wrong guesses from the same IP locks that IP out for 10 minutes.
- **Budget:** the server prices every call from the token counts it gets back and saves the total in `data/usage.json`. Once `BUDGET_USD` is used up, it refuses AI calls. Before each call it sets aside that call's worst-case cost (about $0.50 at the default settings), so even calls running in parallel can't push you over the cap. The HUD shows `$spent / $budget`.
- **No key yet?** `MOCK=1 npm start` replies with a canned build, so you can test everything else.

**Models:** the default is `PROVIDER=gemini` with `gemini-4-argon`. It needs a paid-tier key from [AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey); the free tier returns a "not found" error. Argon costs $2 in / $10 out per million tokens until 2026-11-30, then $4 / $20. The budget tracker switches to the new price on that date by itself. `EFFORT` / `AGENT_EFFORT` set Argon's thinking level (`low|medium|high`). For Claude instead, set `PROVIDER=anthropic` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; the model then defaults to `claude-opus-5-5`, and Claude's safety-check fallbacks are enabled. The AI only runs when a player asks: a ✨ request, an `@Ada …` message, or using an AI-made item or block that calls `ask_ai`. There are no background turns.

## Play

| key | |
|---|---|
| **G** | ✨ ask the AI for anything: "a wizard tower here", "a pet dragon that breathes fire", "a block that heals me", "make it night and spawn ghosts" |
| T / Enter | chat. `@Ada build me a lighthouse` talks to an agent. `/help` lists commands (`/undo`, `/spawn`, `/give`, `/time night`, `/god`, `/new`…) |
| E | inventory: every block, item and creature, including the ones the AI made |
| F | fly · WASD/Space/Shift move · left click break/attack · right click place/use/interact · K agents on/off |

The world saves to the browser's localStorage. Each player has their own world, but everyone shares the AI password and budget.

## How it works: a fe
